https://punchng.com/2027-inec-to-publish.summary: The Independent National Electoral Commission will publish an updated list of candidates for the 2027 general elections following the conclusion of its review process. Amupitan said the review was conducted to address complaints received by the commission, including spelling errors in candidates’ names and cases of double nominations. He explained that INEC had allowed the maximum 14-day period for reviewing the list before making the updated version public.
https://punchng.com/2027-inec-to-publish.summary_zh: 独立国家选举委员会将在审查程序结束后公布2027年大选候选人的更新名单。阿穆皮坦表示，审查旨在处理委员会收到的投诉，包括候选人姓名拼写错误和重复提名的情况。他解释说，独立国家选举委员会已给予审查名单的最长14天期限，之后才公布更新版本。
https://punchng.com/2027-inec-to-publish.body: The Independent National Electoral Commission will publish an updated list of candidates for the 2027 general elections following the conclusion of its review process. INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, SAN, disclosed this on Tuesday in Gombe while speaking with journalists on the sidelines of an interactive session with commission staff from the North-East zone. Amupitan said the review was conducted to address complaints received by the commission, including spelling errors in candidates’ names and cases of double nominations. He explained that INEC had allowed the maximum 14-day period for reviewing the list before making the updated version public. “As you know, usually, in any list published, there could be errors here and there, and there have been complaints of misspelling of names. We have also received complaints of double nominations. “We decided to allow the maximum period of 14 days. Any moment from now, we will make the review public, and the list will be released,” he said. Amupitan’s disclosure comes amid preparations for the 2027 general elections, as the commission continues its review of candidates’ information ahead of the polls
https://punchng.com/2027-inec-to-publish.title_zh: 2027年：独立国家选举委员会将在审核后公布更新后的候选人名单
https://punchng.com/2027-inec-to-publish.body_zh: 独立国家选举委员会将在完成审查程序后，公布2027年大选更新后的候选人名单。独立国家选举委员会主席乔阿什·阿穆皮坦教授（SAN）周二在贡贝向记者透露了這一消息。当时，他正在与委员会东北地区的职员举行互动活动，并在活动间隙接受记者采访。阿穆皮坦表示，此次审查旨在处理委员会收到的投诉，包括候选人姓名拼写错误和重复提名等情况。他解释说，独立国家选举委员会允许利用最长14天时间审查名单，然后公布更新版本。他说：“如你所知，任何公布的名单通常都可能存在这样或那样的错误，我们也收到了有关姓名拼写错误的投诉。此外，还有人投诉存在重复提名。我们决定利用最长14天时间完成审查。我们随时都会公布审查结果并发布名单。”在2027年大选筹备工作之际，独立国家选举委员会正继续审查候选人的信息，为投票做好准备

https://leadership.ng/tinubu-knows-price.summary: Essiet, Senior Special Assistant to the President on Community Engagement in the North-Central region, made this known on Tuesday while speaking with State House correspondents at the Presidential Villa in Abuja. Essiet further stressed that the regular briefings keep Tinubu informed about the cost of basic commodities. Regarding infrastructure development, the presidential aide cited the planned reconstruction of the Mokwa-Bida road in Niger State as an example of efforts to address residents’ concerns.
https://leadership.ng/tinubu-knows-price.summary_zh: 总统负责中北区社区事务的特别助理Essiet周二在阿布贾总统别墅接受州府记者采访时透露了上述情况。Essiet进一步强调，定期简报让Tinubu了解基本生活用品的价格。在基础设施 development 方面，这名总统助理以计划重建尼日尔州Mokwa-Bida公路为例，说明政府为解决居民关切而采取的措施。
https://leadership.ng/tinubu-knows-price.body: Essiet, Senior Special Assistant to the President on Community Engagement in the North-Central region, made this known on Tuesday while speaking with State House correspondents at the Presidential Villa in Abuja. She explained that the President receives regular briefings on the living conditions of Nigerians through community engagement activities and members of the Federal Executive Council. “I don’t feel it’s only media people who understand what the people are facing. Some of the realities our people are experiencing are what we communicate to Mr President,” she said. Essiet further stressed that the regular briefings keep Tinubu informed about the cost of basic commodities. “I usually tell people, you think Mr President doesn’t know the price of egg or bread in the market? He does, because we brief him regularly, and so do members of the Federal Executive Council,” she stated. Regarding infrastructure development, the presidential aide cited the planned reconstruction of the Mokwa-Bida road in Niger State as an example of efforts to address residents’ concerns. She said the road had remained in poor condition for decades, with residents repeatedly calling on the Federal Government to intervene. According to her, the road was last reconstructed 46 years ago, and its deteriorating condition has contributed to fatal accidents involving motorists and heavy-duty vehicles. “The last time that road was given out on contract was 46 years ago. So tell me if that is not the wish of the people,” she said. Essiet also disclosed that Tinubu had directed that the road be reconstructed with reinforced concrete rather than conventional asphalt to improve its durability. “Mr President said they should award the contract and make sure that the contract will be reinforced concrete, not just asphalt,” she added. Meanwhile, Vice President Kashim Shettima expressed optimism on October 19 that food prices would decline in the coming weeks, citing Federal Government efforts to address challenges affecting agricultural production. Shettima made the remarks at a forum titled Together Till 2027: An Evening with Original City Boy , organised by the City Boy Movement alongside the Relax-Tinubu-Is-Fixing-Nigeria movement, both of which support Tinubu’s re-election bid. https://leadership.ng/tinubu-knows-price.title_zh: 总统助理称，蒂努布了解鸡蛋和面包的价格
https://leadership.ng/tinubu-knows-price.body_zh: 总统负责北部和中部分地区社区互动的特别助理高级顾问Essiet周二在阿布贾总统别墅接受国家宫记者采访时透露了这一情况。她解释说，总统通过社区互动活动以及联邦执行委员会成员定期了解尼日利亚人的生活状况。她说：“我不认为只有媒体人士了解民众正在面临的困境。我们向总统先生传达了民众正在经历的一些现实情况。”Essiet进一步强调，定期简报让Tinubu了解基本商品的价格。她说：“我通常会告诉人们，你们以为总统先生不知道市场上鸡蛋或面包的价格吗？他知道，因为我们定期向他汇报，联邦执行委员会成员也这样做。”在基础设施发展方面，这名总统助理以计划重建尼日利亚州Mokwa-Bida公路为例，说明政府为回应居民诉求所作的努力。她说，这条公路几十年来一直状况不佳，居民多次呼吁联邦政府介入。据她介绍，这条公路最后一次重建是在46年前，此后不断恶化的路况已导致涉及小汽车和重型车辆的车祸死亡。她说：“那条公路最后一次承包出去是在46年前。所以你告诉我，这难道不是民众的愿望吗？”Essiet还透露，Tinubu已指示采用钢筋混凝土而非传统沥青重建该公路，以提高其耐久性。她补充道：“总统先生说，应该把合同承包出去，并确保工程采用钢筋混凝土，而不只是沥青。”与此同时，副总统Kashim Shettima于10月19日对食品价格将在未来几周下降表示乐观，并提到联邦政府正在努力解决影响农业生产的问题。Shettimi是在一场题为《共同奋斗至2027年：与Original City Boy共度夜晚》的论坛上作出上述表态的。该论坛由City Boy Movement与Relax-Tinubu-Is-Fixing-Nigeria movement共同组织，这两个组织都支持Tinubu竞选连任。我们掌握独家优势。获取实时报道、突发新闻和独家视角，直接推送到您的手机。不要满足于陈旧新闻。加入LEADERSHIP NEWS的WhatsApp，随时随地获取全天候更新 →

https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.title: Hanwha Defense USA to take control of Philly Shipyard in internal restructuring
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.summary: WASHINGTON — Hanwha Defense USA (HDUSA) said Tuesday it will acquire a controlling stake in Hanwha Philly Shipyard, part of a broader internal restructuring aimed at strengthening the South Korean conglomerate's U.S. naval shipbuilding operations. Under a restructuring plan announced in September, Hanwha Systems Co. will sell its 60 percent stake in the shipyard to Hanwha Defense USA Shipbuilding LLC, a joint venture involving HDUSA and Hanwha FutureProof.
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.summary_zh: 华盛顿——韩华防务美国公司（HDUSA）周二表示，将收购韩华费城造船厂的控股权。这是韩国大型综合企业集团为加强其美国海军造船业务而进行的更广泛内部重组的一部分。根据9月公布的重组计划，韩华系统株式会社将把其在该造船厂持有的60%股份出售给韩华防务美国造船有限责任公司。后者是由HDUSA与韩华FutureProof组成的合资企业。
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.body: WASHINGTON — Hanwha Defense USA (HDUSA) said Tuesday it will acquire a controlling stake in Hanwha Philly Shipyard, part of a broader internal restructuring aimed at strengthening the South Korean conglomerate's U.S. naval shipbuilding operations. Under a restructuring plan announced in September, Hanwha Systems Co. will sell its 60 percent stake in the shipyard to Hanwha Defense USA Shipbuilding LLC, a joint venture involving HDUSA and Hanwha FutureProof. Hanwha Ocean Co. will retain its 40 percent stake. HDUSA said the move will bring the Philadelphia-based shipyard under its leadership as Hanwha seeks to transform the facility into a dual-use shipyard capable of building vessels for the U.S. Navy and commercial customers. "As HDUSA continues to grow its multi-domain presence across the U.S., bringing the Philly Shipyard under HDUSA will further align our government and commercial shipbuilding efforts," HDUSA President and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Michael Coulter said in a statement. Retired U.S. Navy Rear Adm. Tom Anderson, president of U.S. shipbuilding at HDUSA, will oversee the company's American shipbuilding operations as it prepares the facility to serve military and commercial customers. South Korea's Hanwha Group acquired the Philadelphia shipyard in December 2024 as part of its push into the U.S. shipbuilding market, with the latest restructuring aimed at consolidating its defense and shipbuilding capabilities in the country
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.title_zh: Hanwha Defense USA内部重组后将接管费城造船厂
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.body_zh: 华盛顿——Hanwha Defense USA（HDUSA）周二表示，将收购Hanwha Philly Shipyard的控股权。这是该韩国大型集团为加强其美国海军造船业务而进行的更广泛内部重组的一部分。根据9月公布的重组计划，Hanwha Systems Co.将把其持有的该船厂60%股份出售给Hanwha Defense USA Shipbuilding LLC。该合资企业由HDUSA和Hanwha FutureProof共同组建。Hanwha Ocean Co.将保留40%股份。HDUSA表示，此举将使这家总部位于费城的船厂纳入其领导之下。Hanwha正寻求将该设施改造成一座两用船厂，既能建造美国海军舰船，也能满足商业客户需求。HDUSA总裁兼首席执行官Michael Coulter在一份声明中表示：“随着HDUSA继续扩大其在美国的多领域布局，将Philly Shipyard纳入HDUSA将进一步协调我们的政府与商业造船业务。”已退役的美国海军少将Tom Anderson担任HDUSA美国造船业务总裁。随着该船厂准备同时服务军事和商业客户，他将负责监督公司的美国造船业务。韩国Hanwha Group于2024年12月收购这家费城船厂，作为其进军美国造船市场的一部分。此次最新重组旨在整合该集团在该国的国防与造船能力。

https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffa.summary: North Korean officials have paid tribute at the Friendship Tower in Pyongyang in honor of fallen Chinese soldiers, state media reported Monday, after leader Kim Jong-un's surprise day trip to China's Dandong last week. The Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) said senior officials laid wreaths at the monument Sunday to mark the 76th anniversary of the Chinese People's Volunteers' entry into the 1950-53 Korean War.
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffa.summary_zh: 据朝鲜官方媒体周一报道，朝鲜官员在平壤友谊塔向阵亡中国军人敬献花圈，以纪念他们。此前，朝鲜领导人Kim Jong-un于上周突袭访问中国丹东。朝鲜中央通讯社（KCNA）称，高级官员于周日在纪念碑前敬献花圈，纪念中国志愿军参加1950—53年朝鲜战争76周年。
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffa.body: North Korean officials have paid tribute at the Friendship Tower in Pyongyang in honor of fallen Chinese soldiers, state media reported Monday, after leader Kim Jong-un's surprise day trip to China's Dandong last week. The Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) said senior officials laid wreaths at the monument Sunday to mark the 76th anniversary of the Chinese People's Volunteers' entry into the 1950-53 Korean War. Among them were Kim Hyong-sik, vice chairman of the Supreme People's Assembly standing committee, and Vice Foreign Minister Kim Myong-su. They were joined by Chinese embassy officials, including Qi Han, charge d'affaires ad interim, and a Chinese delegation led by Hong Zongming, vice minister of China's veterans affairs ministry. Wreaths were also laid at cemeteries and graves of Chinese soldiers in Anju, Hoechang County, Onsong County and Kaesong. The Chinese side hosted a reception later Sunday to mark the anniversary, the report added. The North Korean leader traveled to the Chinese border city of Dandong on Saturday, a trip meant to showcase the decades-old alliance with China and mark the anniversary. He visited a war memorial to Chinese soldiers who fought in the Korean War, attended a banquet and toured a bus factory
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffa.title_zh: 朝鲜官员在友谊塔向牺牲的中国军人致祭

https://leadership.ng/just-in-fg-approve.title: JUST IN: FG Approves N70,000 Monthly Transport Allowance For Workers
https://leadership.ng/just-in-fg-approve.summary: The Federal Government has approved a N70,000 monthly transport intervention for public service workers across all levels for six months, beginning in November 2026, to cushion the impact of rising living costs. The approval was one of the resolutions reached at a conciliation meeting between the Federal Government and the leadership of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) in Abuja on Tuesday, following renewed pressure from organised labour over the rising cost of living, workers’ welfare and outstanding agreements.
https://leadership.ng/just-in-fg-approve.summary_zh: 联邦政府已批准从2026年11月起，连续6个月向各级公共服务人员每月发放7万奈拉交通补贴，以缓解生活成本上涨带来的影响。这是联邦政府与尼日利亚劳工大会（NLC）领导层周二在阿布贾召开调解会议后达成的决议之一。此前，有组织劳工因生活成本上涨、工人福利及尚未履行的协议而再次向政府施压。
https://leadership.ng/just-in-fg-approve.body: The Federal Government has approved a N70,000 monthly transport intervention for public service workers across all levels for six months, beginning in November 2026, to cushion the impact of rising living costs. The approval was one of the resolutions reached at a conciliation meeting between the Federal Government and the leadership of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) in Abuja on Tuesday, following renewed pressure from organised labour over the rising cost of living, workers’ welfare and outstanding agreements. The government also approved the payment of peculiar allowance arrears, effective from May 1, 2026, in three equal monthly instalments beginning in November. However, the meeting ended without an agreement on the effective date for implementing the national minimum wage. https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.body: A bank official on Tuesday gave details of security funds the Sambo Dasuki-led Office of the National Security Adviser (ONSA) received from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) and the Office of the Accountant General of the Federation in 2015, and how the funds were transferred to various beneficiaries. Arhyel Mshelia, a compliance officer with Access Bank, testified before the FCT High Court in Maitama as the third prosecution witness in an over-a-decade-long N4.6 billion arms procurement fraud trial case involving Mr Dasuki. Mr Mshelia narrated how the security funds made their ways into the accounts of Jabbama Ada Global Services, Jawas Multipurpose Ventures and Onile Nigeria Limited in 2015. Mr Dasuki has been standing trial in the case since 2015 alongside former Sokoto State Governor Attahiru Bafarawa, his son Sagir Bafarawa, former Minister of State for Finance Bashir Yuguda, and Dalhatu Investment Limited. Mr Dasuki and his co-defendants are facing 25 counts of misappropriation, criminal breach of trust and receiving stolen property. The charges accuse them of diverting N4.6 billion from the NSA office’s account. The money was said to be meant for procurement of arms to firm up the offensive against Boko Haram terrorists during former President Goodluck Jonathan administration, between 2014 and 2015. Going through the statement of the ONSA’s account on Tuesday, the witness informed the court that the former NSA, Mr Dasuki, and one Salisu Abdulmalik Shaibu used to be signatories to the account with Access Bank. Arhyel said on 16 March 2015, there was an inflow credit of N500 million from the CBN; the amount was disbursed on 25 March, 2015. Similarly, the account was credited with N5 billion on 10 April 2015. On 16 April 2015, N27 million and N400 million were sent to Jabbama Ada Global Limited. The signatory to Jabbama Ada was Salisu Umar Garu, the witness said. He also said Jabbama Ada received N500 million on 5 February 2015 and N1 billion on 16 April 2015 from the ONSA’s office. From the Federation Allocation Account Committee’s (FAAC’s) account with the OAGF, the company received N38 million and N25 million on 6 and 7 January 2015, respectively and N55 million on 5 February 2015. According to the witness, Onile Nigeria Limited, whose signatory is Tom Ikimi, received N200 million and N100 million from ONSA on 9 and 18 February 2015. Jawas Multipurpose Ventures also received N2 billion, he said. During cross-examination by the defence, the witness said he did not know the purpose of the transactions. He also disclosed that Jabbama Ada was involved in general contracts, oil and gas, purchase and resale of lands and transport. Fielding questions from Mr Yuguda and Dalhatu Investment Limited’s lawyer, James Olatoke, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN), the witness said he did not know of any relationship between Jabbama Ada and his clients. He also noted transfers from other individuals and companies aside from the ONSA and CBN. The first prosecution witness, Hamza Abdullahi, who served as the second-in-command of the EFCC’s Special Task Force that investigated the alleged arms procurement fraud in the NSA office, had testified that N4.633 billion was traced to Dalhatu Investment Limited. He said Mr Sagir, the son of the former Sokoto governor, is the company’s sole account signatory. The second prosecution witness, Mr Yusuf, had also testified that funds were released from the NSA office for the supply of security equipment but that the contracts were not executed. He said that during the investigation, Mr Sagir brought a list showing how the funds were used. The witness said the funds were used to sponsor pilgrimage to Mecca and partly used for the 2015 political campaigns of the then-ruling party, the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP). He listed the recipients of the funds to include Sheikh AbdurRahman Al-Sudais Foundation (N500 million), belonging to former Governor Bafarawa, and 2015 Sokoto PDP governorship candidate, Abdallah Wali, who allegedly received N580 million through a company. The case is one of the twin arms procurement fraud matters filed against Mr Dasuki and his co-defendants over the streams of funds he released from NSA office accounts between 2014 and 2015. In the other trial, the EFCC is prosecuting Mr Dasuki, a retired colonel, alongside a former General Manager at the Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC), Aminu Baba-Kusa; Acacia Holdings Limited; and Reliance Referral Hospital Limited on 32 counts of fraud involving diversion of N33.2 billion arms funds entrusted to the NSA office. In March, the EFCC re-arraigned the defendants on criminal breach of trust, among other charges, following the reassignment of the case that started in 2015 to a new judge, Charles Agbaza. The defendants denied all charges as they did when they were first arraigned in 2015. The two cases suffered multiple adjournments in their early years, largely due to the State Security Services (SSS) refusing to release Mr Dasuki on bail despite multiple court orders. Mr Dasuki served as NSA between 2012 and 2015, at the height of Boko Haram attacks in Nigeria’s North-east, during the administration of then-President Goodluck Jonathan. An audit panel set up by the administration of President Muhammadu Buhari, who came to office after defeating Mr Jonathan in the 2015 presidential election, revealed that about $2 billion entrusted to the office of the NSA, then led by Mr Dasuki, for procurement of arms could not be accounted for. The EFCC, which instituted multiple charges against diverse persons who received funds from the NSA office, alleged that the arms funds were doled out to friends, relatives, political allies, particularly members of the PDP, for purposes unrelated to the purchase of arms
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.title_zh: 达苏基任内的国家安全办公室如何支付从尼日利亚中央银行获得的安保资金，审计长揭开内幕
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.body_zh: 一名银行官员周二披露了由桑博·达苏基领导的国家安全顾问办公室（ONSA）于2015年从尼日利亚中央银行（CBN）和联邦总会计师办公室收到的安全资金明细，以及这些资金如何转给 various 受益人。Access Bank合规官Arhyel Mshelia在迈塔马联邦首都特区高等法院作证，作为涉及达苏基先生、历时十余年的46亿奈拉军火采购欺诈案的第三名控方案件证人。Mshelia先生讲述了这些安全资金如何在2015年进入Jabbama Ada Global Services、Jawas Multipurpose Ventures和Onile Nigeria Limited的账户。达苏基先生自2015年以来一直与前索科托州长阿塔希鲁·巴法拉瓦、其子萨吉尔·巴法拉瓦、前财政部国务部长巴希尔·尤古达及Dalhatu Investment Limited一起就该案受审。达苏基先生及其共同被告面临25项挪用、违反信任罪和接收盗窃财产罪指控。指控称，他们将46亿奈拉从国家安全局办公室的账户中挪用。这笔钱据称用于采购武器，以加强前总统古德勒克·乔纳森执政期间，即2014年至2015年间，对博科哈拉姆恐怖分子的进攻。证人周二核查ONSA账户对账单后向法院表示，前国家安全顾问达苏基先生和Salisu Abdulmalik Shaibu曾是该账户在Access Bank的签字人。Arhyel称，2015年3月16日，账户收到来自CBN的5亿奈拉入账；这笔钱于2015年3月25日支出。同样，该账户于2015年4月10日收到50亿奈拉。2015年4月16日，2700万奈拉和4亿奈拉被转给Jabbama Ada Global Limited。证人称，Jabbama Ada的签字人是Salisu Umar Garu。他还表示，Jabbama Ada于2015年2月5日和4月16日分别从ONSA办公室收到5亿奈拉和10亿奈拉。从联邦拨款账户委员会（FAAC）在OAGF的账户中，该公司于2015年1月6日和7日分别收到3800万奈拉和2500万奈拉，并于2015年2月5日收到5500万奈拉。据证人称，Onile Nigeria Limited的签字人为Tom Ikimi，该公司于2015年2月9日和18日分别从ONSA收到2亿奈拉和1亿奈拉。他说，Jawas Multipurpose Ventures也收到了20亿奈拉。在辩方交叉询问期间，证人表示他不知道这些交易的用途。他还披露，除ONSA和CBN外，其他个人和公司也向相关账户转过款。第一名控方案件证人Hamza Abdullahi曾担任经济和金融犯罪委员会（EFCC）调查国家安全局办公室涉嫌军火采购欺诈案特别行动组的副指挥官。他曾作证称，有46.33亿奈拉被追踪到Dalhatu Investment Limited。他说，前索科托州长的儿子萨吉尔先生是该公司的唯一账户签字人。第二名控方案件证人优素福先生也曾作证称，国家安全局办公室曾为供应安全设备拨付资金，但合同并未履行。他说，在调查期间，萨吉尔先生提交了一份资金使用清单。证人称，这些资金被用于赞助赴麦加朝觐，并部分用于当时的执政党人民民主党（PDP）的2015年竞选活动。他列出的资金受益者包括属于前州长巴法拉瓦的Sheikh AbdurRahman Al-Sudais Foundation（5亿奈拉），以及据称通过一家公司获得5.8亿奈拉的2015年索科托州PDP州长候选人阿卜杜拉·瓦利。该案是针对达苏基先生及其共同被告提起的两起关联军火采购欺诈案之一，案件涉及其于2014年至2015年间从国家安全局办公室账户拨出的多笔资金。在另一场审判中，EFCC以32项欺诈罪起诉已退役上校达苏基先生及尼日利亚国家石油公司（NNPC）前总经理Aminu Baba-Kusa、Acacia Holdings Limited和Reliance Referral Hospital Limited，涉案内容为挪用受托交给国家安全局办公室的332亿奈拉军火资金。3月，在该案自2015年启动后改由新法官Charles Agbaza审理之际，EFCC以违反信任罪等罪名重新提请审判被告。被告否认了全部指控，与2015年首次受审时一样。这两起案件在最初几年多次延期，主要原因是尽管法院多次下达命令，国家安全局（SSS）仍拒绝保释放达苏基先生。达苏基先生于2012年至2015年担任国家安全顾问，当时正值古德勒克·乔纳森总统执政期间、尼日利亚东北部博科哈拉姆袭击最严重的时候。穆罕马杜·布哈里总统执政后设立了一个审计小组。布哈里在2015年总统选举中击败乔纳森先生后就任。由该审计小组披露，约有20亿美元受托交给当时由达苏基先生领导的国家安全局办公室用于采购武器的资金无法说明去向。EFCC对多名从国家安全局办公室收取资金的人提起多项指控，称这些军火资金被发放给朋友、亲属和政治盟友，尤其是PDP成员，用于与购买武器无关的目的……

https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.body: The House of Representatives has urged the federal government to establish a transparent framework for the importation of electric vehicles (EVs), compressed natural gas (CNG) vehicles and other clean mobility equipment into Nigeria. The call followed a motion moved by Ademorin Kuye (APC, Lagos) during Tuesday’s plenary in Abuja. Moving the motion, Mr Kuye said Nigeria has adopted policies that promote the transition to EVs, CNG vehicles, liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) vehicles, and other clean transportation technologies as part of its energy transition and economic diversification agenda. He said the government had introduced fiscal incentives, including import duty and tax reliefs, to encourage investment in clean mobility technologies and expand charging infrastructure and CNG refuelling stations. He said the policy’s success would also depend on the availability of maintenance centres, spare parts, technical expertise, and after-sales support. Mr Kuye said Nigeria could use the import incentives to encourage local investment, technology transfer, employment generation and domestic value addition by linking the incentives to measurable investments in infrastructure and technical capacity. “Nigeria has the opportunity to encourage local investment, technology transfer, employment generation, and domestic value addition by linking import incentives to measurable investments in infrastructure and technical capacity,” he said. He urged the federal government to establish a transparent licensing and approval framework for the commercial importation of EVs, CNG vehicles and related clean mobility equipment. He also urged the National Automotive Design and Development Council (NADDC), in collaboration with the Bureau of Public Procurement (BPP), Standards Organisation of Nigeria (SON), Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) and other relevant agencies, to develop objective criteria for approving importers. Under the proposed framework, companies seeking approval would, where applicable, be required to establish certified service and maintenance centres in Nigeria, provide genuine spare parts and warranty support, and employ and train qualified Nigerian technical personnel. They would also be required to invest in EV charging infrastructure or CNG refuelling facilities, comply with Nigerian safety, environmental and technical standards, and submit consumer protection and after-sales service plans. The lawmaker further urged the NADDC to maintain a public register of approved importers and infrastructure providers to promote transparency and consumer confidence. He said the approval process must remain open, competitive, and non-discriminatory, allowing any company that meets the prescribed standards to obtain approval without undue preference. He also urged the government to align tax incentives, import duty concessions, and other fiscal benefits with the proposed regulatory framework to encourage sustained investment in local infrastructure. Contributing to the debate, Dominic Okafor (APGA, Anambra) supported the motion, saying importers should be required to provide after-sales support, maintenance centres and spare parts to protect consumers. Adedeji Olajide (APM, Oyo) said greenhouse gas emissions contribute to global warming and argued that an appropriate framework for electric mobility would help Nigeria develop a more environmentally friendly transport system and contribute to global efforts to address climate change. Sada Soli (APC, Katsina) said legislation was required to provide clear guidelines for implementing the policy. The House unanimously adopted the motion after Speaker Abbas Tajudeen subjected it to a voice vote. It then asked the NADDC, BPP, SON, NCS, and other relevant agencies to develop objective qualification criteria for approving the importation of EVs, CNG vehicles, and related clean mobility equipment. The House Committees on Industry, Commerce, Gas Resources, Environment and Legislative Compliance were also mandated to monitor implementation and report back within four weeks for further legislative action. CNG is natural gas compressed to high pressure and used as vehicle fuel. It is generally considered a cleaner-burning alternative to petrol and diesel because it produces lower levels of some pollutants and greenhouse gas emissions
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.title_zh: 议员要求为电动汽车和压缩天然气汽车进口建立透明框架
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.body_zh: 众议院敦促联邦政府为电动汽车（EV）、压缩天然气（CNG）车辆及其他清洁出行设备进口至尼日利亚建立透明框架。此项呼吁源于阿德莫林·库耶（APC，拉各斯州议员）在阿布贾星期二全体会议上提出的动议。库耶先生提出动议时表示，尼日利亚已采纳相关政策，推动向电动汽车、CNG车辆、液化石油气（LPG）车辆及其他清洁交通技术转型，作为其能源转型和经济多元化议程的一部分。他说，政府已推出财政激励措施，包括进口关税和税收减免，以鼓励对清洁出行技术的投资，并扩大充电基础设施和CNG加气站。他表示，这项政策能否成功还取决于维修中心、备件、技术专长和售后支持的可用性。库耶先生说，尼日利亚可以利用进口激励措施，通过将激励与基础设施及技术能力方面的可量化投资挂钩，鼓励本地投资、技术转让、就业创造和国内价值增值。他说：“尼日利亚有机会通过将进口激励措施与基础设施及技术能力方面的可量化投资挂钩，鼓励本地投资、技术转让、就业创造和国内价值增值。”他敦促联邦政府为商业进口电动汽车、CNG车辆及相关清洁出行设备建立透明的许可和审批框架。他还敦促国家汽车设计与开发委员会（NADDC）与公共采购局（BPP）、尼日利亚标准组织（SON）、尼日利亚海关总署（NCS）及其他相关机构合作，制定审批进口商的客观标准。根据拟议框架，申请审批的公司在适用情况下，须在尼日利亚设立经认证的服务和维修中心，提供正品备件和保修支持，并雇用和培训合格的尼日利亚技术人员。公司还须投资建设电动汽车充电基础设施或CNG加气设施，遵守尼日利亚安全、环境和技术标准，并提交消费者保护及售后服务计划。该议员进一步敦促NADDC维护获批进口商和基础设施供应商的公开名册，以促进透明度和消费者信心。他说，审批流程必须保持公开、竞争和非歧视性，使任何符合规定标准的公司都能获得审批，而不得给予不当优待。他还敦促政府使税收激励、进口关税优惠及其他财政利益与拟议监管框架相衔接，以鼓励对本地基础设施的持续投资。Dominic Okafor（APGA，阿南布拉州议员）参与讨论并支持该动议，称应要求进口商提供售后支持、维修中心和备件，以保护消费者。Adedeji Olajide（APM，奥约州议员）表示，温室气体排放会加剧全球变暖，并认为适当的电动汽车出行框架将有助于尼日利亚发展更环保的交通体系，并为全球应对气候变化的努力作出贡献。Sada Soli（APC，卡齐纳州议员）表示，需要通过立法为政策实施提供明确指引。众议院议长Abbas Tajudeen付诸表决后，表决结果为全票通过该动议。众议院随后要求NADDC、BPP、SON、NCS及其他相关机构制定审批进口电动汽车、CNG车辆及相关清洁出行设备的客观资格标准。众议院还授权工业、商业、天然气资源、环境和立法合规委员会监督政策执行情况，并在四周内提交报告，以便采取进一步立法行动。CNG是经高压压缩、用作车辆燃料的天然气。由于其产生的某些污染物和温室气体排放水平较低，通常被认为是比汽油和柴油燃烧更清洁的替代燃料

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/27/s.summary: The Presidency has tasked organised private sector in the country to develop a comprehensive financing and implementation blueprint for the proposed state police system. According to him, the private sector has a direct stake in the success of the reform because insecurity was already imposing enormous costs on businesses through disrupted supply chains, abandoned investments, postponed factory expansions and lost economic opportunities.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/27/s.summary_zh: 总统府已责成全国有组织的私营部门制定拟议中的国家警察体系的综合融资与实施蓝图。据他介绍，私营部门与改革成败直接相关，因为不安全局势已经通过供应链中断、投资搁置、工厂扩建延期和经济机会流失，给企业带来巨大成本。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/27/s.body: The Presidency has tasked organised private sector in the country to develop a comprehensive financing and implementation blueprint for the proposed state police system. It stated that businesses must take an active role in building the security institutions required to protect investments, create jobs and strengthen economic resilience. Chief of Staff to the President and Chairman of the Presidential Working Group on the National Policing Bill, Hon. Femi Gbajabiamila, who gave the challenge, particularly charged the Nigerian Economic Summit Group (NESG), chambers of commerce and business associations with producing practical proposals for financing, institutional management and accountable partnerships to support the decentralisation of policing. According to him, the private sector has a direct stake in the success of the reform because insecurity was already imposing enormous costs on businesses through disrupted supply chains, abandoned investments, postponed factory expansions and lost economic opportunities. Speaking during a plenary session on “Security, Stability and Economic Resilience” at the 32nd Nigerian Economic Summit in Abuja, Gbajabiamila said President Bola Tinubu’s commitment to establishing state police presented an opportunity for businesses to contribute directly to the development of security institutions capable of supporting sustainable economic growth. “I therefore ask the Nigerian Economic Summit Group to carry this engagement beyond our meeting. Bring forward a considered private sector contribution on financing and implementing state police, with practical proposals for accountable partnerships. “Take that work into the legislative process and into your engagement with state governments. For our part, we remain answerable for turning reform into protection that people can rely on,” he said. Gbajabiamila urged business leaders to engage governors and legislators on the proposed reform, drawing attention to the relationship between effective local policing, employment generation and investment decisions. He explained that the experience of businesses in managing institutions, controlling expenditure and assessing risks could strengthen the design and implementation of the new policing framework. According to him, the organised private sector should also provide evidence of security failures preventing otherwise viable investments from proceeding, enabling policymakers to determine where additional security capacity was most urgently required. “His words: “Your participation should also improve the substance of the reform. As the legislative process proceeds, examine the proposals for financing and oversight. “Bring your experience of managing institutions and controlling expenditure to that discussion. Help us understand the security failures that prevent viable projects from proceeding.” The Chief of Staff, however, cautioned that private sector involvement must be transparent and should never compromise the independence of police institutions. He said businesses could contribute expertise in communications infrastructure, equipment maintenance and financial planning, but insisted that such partnerships must operate within clearly defined legal and accountability frameworks. “Where businesses provide resources, those contributions need published accounts and independent scrutiny. “Public funding must remain dependable, and a donation must never purchase influence over an investigation or preferential treatment. The object is to strengthen a public service on which every citizen can rely,” he warned. Gbajabiamila explained that the administration was determined to establish financially sustainable state police institutions, insisting that states seeking to operate their own services must demonstrate the capacity to meet recurrent expenditure obligations. According to him, providing vehicles, uniforms and other equipment at the commencement of operations would be insufficient without sustainable arrangements for personnel salaries, professional training and operational maintenance. “Financial readiness is equally important. A state taking on policing must be able to sustain the service after the initial purchase of vehicles and uniforms. “Regular pay and continued training are essential to professional conduct. An institution that cannot meet its obligations to its officers becomes vulnerable to private patrons and unlawful demands on the public,” he cautioned. The Chief of Staff assured that federal policing would continue in states not yet financially or institutionally prepared to establish their own police services. Providing an update on the legislative process, Gbajabiamila confirmed that 24 State Houses of Assembly had approved the constitutional amendment providing for state police as at October 23, 2026 meeting the required two-thirds threshold. He disclosed that the Presidential Working Group had submitted the draft National Policing Bill and 29 consequential amendment bills to the Federal Ministry of Justice on October 19 for legislative review. According to him, after the review and the Working Group’s final consideration, the proposals would be presented to President Tinubu for approval before transmission to the National Assembly. He explained that the proposed framework would enable willing and capable states to assume greater responsibility for protecting their residents, while retaining a strong federal police institution to address interstate criminal activities and other specialised national security requirements. Gbajabiamila said the reform was intended to correct the structural imbalance under which state governments were responsible for responding to the consequences of insecurity without possessing corresponding authority to organise policing. “Bringing policing closer to the communities it serves can improve local intelligence and shorten the time between a call for help and an effective response,” he explained. Addressing concerns about the possible deployment of state police against political opponents, he assured Nigerians that the proposed legislation would contain enforceable safeguards, national professional standards and independent oversight mechanisms. “The concern that police powers could be used against political opponents or vulnerable communities is serious. Our answer is to place enforceable limits on those powers and provide remedies when they are abused. “A citizen’s entitlement to protection cannot depend on whom he supports or where she comes from,” the Chief of Staff declared. He said the framework had benefited from consultations with state governments, security institutions, members of the public and a Policy Advisory Committee drawn from the public and private sectors. Explaining why businesses should champion the reform, Gbajabiamila said insecurity affected investment decisions far beyond the immediate financial burden of hiring private security personnel. Said he: “The cost of the present arrangement is already in your accounts. You pay for additional security and disrupted deliveries. “You also bear losses that never appear as a separate charge: a factory expansion postponed, or a productive location excluded from your investment plans.” He argued that companies could not guarantee sustainable operations merely by securing their premises while surrounding communities remained unsafe. According to him: ‘A company can reinforce its perimeter. Its workers still have to travel home, and its suppliers still have to move through the surrounding communities. “Your long-term security depends on the strength of public institutions beyond your gates.” Turning to the administration’s wider security interventions, Gbajabiamila said President Tinubu had supported the modernisation of the Armed Forces through the induction of helicopters into Army Aviation and the restoration of more than 100 refurbished armoured fighting vehicles to active service. He recalled that the President commissioned three additional naval vessels in June to strengthen maritime security, noting that sustained operations against crude oil theft had contributed to improved oil production, foreign exchange earnings and government revenues. On food security, the Chief of Staff disclosed that the deployment of 10,000 Agro-Rangers across 19 states and the Federal Capital Territory was helping to integrate agricultural production with security protection. He explained that the administration recognised that investments in improved seedlings, agricultural credit and other support programmes would achieve little without guaranteeing farmers’ access to their land. “Improved seedlings and access to credit will achieve little on farmland that its owners are afraid to cultivate. Protection makes those agricultural interventions usable,” he said. Gbajabiamila also highlighted the Presidential Forest Guards Initiative, under which more than 7,000 personnel drawn from seven frontline states had completed training by December 2025 to support security operations in areas exploited by criminal groups. He disclosed that President Tinubu had directed the preparation of a National Threat Assessment and a rolling five-year Strategic Defence Operations Plan in August to improve coordination, align security spending with operational priorities and strengthen institutional accountability. Acknowledging that Nigerians continued to face threats of kidnapping and violent attacks despite government investments in security, he said the administration recognised that its achievements must ultimately be measured by the safety of citizens. “Nigerians living with the threat of abduction or attack are entitled to judge us by their own safety. We recognise the distance between an improvement in national capacity and dependable protection in every community.” The Chief of Staff further linked the administration’s security interventions with its economic reform programme, including fuel subsidy removal, foreign exchange restructuring and tax reforms. He acknowledged that the reforms had imposed considerable pressure on households and businesses but maintained that economic productivity and security were mutually dependent. “A government with inadequate revenues cannot sustain the institutions required to protect its citizens. An economy in which people cannot work safely cannot generate the revenues government needs. “We have therefore had to address both problems together, even as the costs of transition have placed considerable pressure on Nigerian households and businesses,” the Chief of Staff explained. Gbajabiamila urged investors to respond to improving security conditions by returning to communities where commercial activities had been disrupted, arguing that renewed investments would create employment, restore local supply chains and expand public revenues. He assured business leaders that the administration welcomed constructive criticism and practical recommendations, stressing that President Tinubu’s willingness to confront longstanding structural challenges required sustained cooperation from all stakeholders. “A farmer returning to his land and an employer reopening a business will be making decisions about their families’ futures. Our work together must give them sound reasons to proceed.” Founded on January 22, 1995, THISDAY is published by THISDAY NEWSPAPERS LTD., 35 Creek Road Apapa, Lagos, Nigeria with offices in 36 states of Nigeria , the Federal Capital Territory and around the world. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/27/s.body_zh: 总统府已责成全国有组织私营部门为拟议中的州警察制度制定一套全面的融资与实施蓝图。总统府表示，企业必须积极参与建设维护投资、创造就业和增强经济韧性所需的安全机构。总统幕僚长兼国家警务法案总统工作组主席Femi Gbajabiamila阁下提出这一任务，并特别要求尼日利亚经济峰会组织（NESG）、商会和商业协会提出切实可行的融资方案、机构管理方案以及问责伙伴关系，以支持警务权力下放。他说，私营部门与改革成效直接相关，因为不安全状况已通过供应链中断、投资搁置、工厂扩建推迟和经济机会流失，给企业造成巨额成本。Gbajabiamila在阿布贾举行的第32届尼日利亚经济峰会“安全、稳定与经济韧性”全体会议上发言时表示，总统Bola Tinubu推动建立州警察，为企业直接参与建设支撑可持续经济增长的安全机构创造了机会。“因此，我请尼日利亚经济峰会组织把这项工作延伸到本次会议之外。认真提出私营部门关于州警察融资与实施的贡献意见，并就问责伙伴关系提出切实可行的建议。“将这项工作纳入立法进程，以及你们与州政府的沟通之中。就我们而言，我们仍负责把改革转化为公众可以信赖的保护措施。”他说。Gbajabiamila敦促商业领袖就拟议改革与州长和议员沟通，并提请他们关注有效的地方警务、创造就业与投资决策之间的关系。他解释称，企业管理机构、控制支出和评估风险的经验，可以强化新警务框架的设计与实施。他说，有组织私营部门还应提供安全失灵导致原本可行的投资无法推进的证据，使政策制定者能够确定哪里最迫切需要增加安全能力。“他的话是：“你们的参与还应提升改革的实质内容。随着立法进程推进，请审查有关融资和监督的各项建议。“请把你们管理机构和控制支出的经验带入讨论，帮助我们了解阻碍可行项目推进的安全失灵问题。”不过，这位幕僚长警告称，私营部门参与必须保持透明，绝不能损害警察机构的独立性。他说，企业可以在通信基础设施、设备维护和财务规划方面贡献专业知识，但此类伙伴关系必须在界限明确的法律和问责框架内运作。“凡是企业提供资源，这些投入都必须公布账目并接受独立审查。“公共资金必须保持稳定可靠，任何捐赠都绝不能换取对调查的影响力或优待待遇。目标是强化一项每位公民都能信赖的公共服务。”他警告道。Gbajabiamila表示，政府决心建立财政上可持续的州警察机构，并强调，希望运营自有警察服务的州必须证明其有能力承担经常性支出义务。他说，行动启动时提供车辆、制服和其他设备并不足够，还必须为人员薪资、专业培训和行动维护作出可持续安排。“财务准备同样重要。一个承担警务任务的州，必须能够在初步购置车辆和制服后继续维持该服务。“按时发放薪酬和持续培训是专业履职的必要条件。一个无法履行对警员义务的机构，会容易受到私人资助方控制以及非法公共要求的侵蚀。”他提醒道。这位幕僚长保证，对于尚未在财政或机构层面做好自建警察服务准备的州，联邦警务仍将继续运作。在介绍立法进程进展时，Gbajabiamila确认，截至2026年10月23日，已有24个州议会批准了关于设立州警察的宪法修正案，达到法定三分之二门槛。他透露，总统工作组已于10月19日向联邦司法部提交《国家警务法案》草案和29项配套修正案，供立法审议。他说，在完成审议和工作组最终审议后，这些提案将提交总统Tinubu批准，再送交国民议会。他解释称，拟议框架将使有意愿且有能力的州承担更多保护本州居民的责任，同时保留强大的联邦警察机构，以应对跨州犯罪活动和其他专业国家安全需求。Gbajabiamila说，这项改革旨在纠正一种结构性失衡，即州政府须应对不安全状况造成的后果，却无权组织警务。“让警务更贴近其服务的社区，可以改善地方情报工作，并缩短从求助到有效响应之间的时间。”他解释道。针对州警察可能被部署用于对付政治对手的担忧，他向尼日利亚人保证，拟议立法将包含可执行的保障措施、国家专业标准和独立监督机制。“警察权力可能被用于对付政治对手或弱势社区，这种担忧十分严肃。我们的应对办法是对这些权力设置可执行的限制，并在权力遭滥用时提供救济。“公民获得保护的权利不能取决于其支持谁或来自哪里。”这位幕僚长宣称。他说，该框架受益于与州政府、安全机构、公众成员以及由公共和私营部门人员组成的政策咨询委员会进行的磋商。Gbajabiamila解释企业为何应支持这项改革时表示，不安全状况对投资决策造成的影响，远远超出雇佣私人保安人员所带来的直接财务负担。他说：“现行安排的成本已经计入你们的账目。你们为额外安保和交付中断付费。“你们还承担从未作为单独费用出现的损失，例如工厂扩建推迟，或某个适宜生产的地点被排除在投资计划之外。”他论证称，如果周边社区仍不安全，企业仅靠保护自身场所无法保障持续运营。他说：“企业可以加强外围防护，但员工仍要回家，供应商仍要经过周边社区。“你们的长期安全取决于大门之外公共机构的力量。”谈及政府更广泛的安全干预措施时，Gbajabiamila表示，总统Tinubu支持通过将直升机列装陆军航空兵以及恢复100多辆经过翻新的装甲战斗车辆投入现役，推动武装部队现代化。他回忆称，总统于6月为其余3艘海军舰艇主持启用，以加强海上安全，并指出，针对原油盗取的持续行动已促进石油产量、外汇收入和政府财政收入增加。在粮食安全方面，这位幕僚长披露，政府已在19个州和联邦首都地区部署10,000名Agro-Rangers，以促进农业生产与安全保障相结合。他解释称，政府认识到，如果不保障农民能够进入自己的土地，对改良种子、农业信贷和其他支持计划的投入将难有成效。“在土地所有者因害怕而不敢耕种的农田上，改良种子和信贷获取都难以发挥作用。安全保障才能使这些农业干预措施真正落地。”Gbajabiamila还强调总统森林守卫倡议，根据该倡议，截至2025年12月，来自7个前线州的7,000多名人员已完成训练，以支持在犯罪团伙活动地区的安全行动。他透露，总统Tinubu已于8月指示编制《国家威胁评估》和滚动五年期《战略防务行动计划》，以改善协调工作、使安全支出与行动重点保持一致，并强化机构问责。Gbajabiamila承认，尽管政府不断增加安全投入，尼日利亚人仍持续面临绑架和暴力袭击威胁，但他表示，政府认识到，其成效最终必须以公民安全来衡量。“生活在绑架或袭击威胁中的尼日利亚人，有权依据自身安全状况评价我们。我们认识到，国家能力提升与每个社区都获得可靠保护之间仍有差距。”这位幕僚长进一步将政府的安全干预与其经济改革计划联系起来，包括取消燃油补贴、外汇结构调整和税收改革。他承认，这些改革给家庭和企业带来了相当大的压力，但坚持认为，经济生产率与安全相互依存。“收入不足的政府无法维持保护公民所需的机构。在人们无法安全工作的情况下，经济也无法创造政府所需的收入。“因此，我们不得不同时处理这两个问题，尽管转型成本已对尼日利亚家庭和企业造成相当大的压力。”这位幕僚长解释道。Gbajabiamila敦促投资者因安全状况改善而重返那些商业活动曾受干扰的地区，并认为，恢复投资将创造就业、恢复本地供应链并扩大公共收入。他向商业领袖保证，政府欢迎建设性批评和切实可行的建议，并强调，总统Tinubu正视长期结构性挑战的意愿，需要所有利益相关方持续合作。“返乡的农民和重新开业的雇主将在为家人的未来作出决定。我们共同的努力必须给他们充分理由继续前进。”THISDAY于1995年1月22日创刊，由THISDAY NEWSPAPERS LTD.出版，社址位于尼日利亚拉各斯阿帕帕克里克路35号，在尼日利亚36个州、联邦首都地区以及世界各地设有办公室。它是尼日利亚最具权威性的新闻媒体，通过全平台面向政治、商业、专业和外交精英及更广泛的中产阶级报道，同时为有抱负者和千禧一代提供新思想、文化与技术的交汇平台。

https://www.premiumtimesng.com/business/.summary: Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals has successfully concluded its landmark Initial Public Offering (IPO), attracting investor applications from 120 countries across all six inhabited continents, including all 54 African countries.
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/business/.summary_zh: 丹格特炼油与石化公司已成功完成其里程碑式首次公开募股（IPO），吸引了来自全球六个有人居住大洲120个国家的投资者申请，其中包括非洲全部54个国家。
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/business/.body: Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals has successfully concluded its landmark Initial Public Offering (IPO), attracting investor applications from 120 countries across all six inhabited continents, including all 54 African countries. In a statement on Tuesday, the company described the development as an unprecedented demonstration of the continent’s capacity to mobilise capital and broaden ownership of strategic industrial assets. The historic offering, widely described as The People’s IPO, achieved 100 per cent geographical coverage of Africa, bringing together investors from across the continent and beyond in a transaction that could redefine the scale, accessibility and international reach of African capital markets. More than a conventional fundraising exercise, the IPO has become a landmark in financial inclusion, showing how digital technology, coordinated financial institutions, and innovative distribution channels can connect millions of potential investors to opportunities previously dominated by institutional and high-net-worth participants. The transaction was supported by an extensive network of commercial banks, stockbroking firms, fintech platforms, capital market institutions and distribution partners, whose collaboration expanded access to the offer across national boundaries and created new pathways for retail participation. For Dangote Industries Limited, the IPO’s conclusion marks a defining moment in its industrial journey, shifting the refinery’s ownership proposition from an investment driven by a single entrepreneurial vision to an opportunity for broader African participation. President and Chief Executive of Dangote Industries Limited, Aliko Dangote, described the outcome as a powerful affirmation of African confidence, enterprise, and the continent’s ability to mobilise its own resources for development. “When we set out to build this refinery, many doubted that a project of this scale could be delivered by Africans. We proved that Africa could build it. Today, through this historic IPO, we have demonstrated something equally important: Africans are ready to own and participate in the prosperity created by their own industries. “To have investor applications from all 54 African countries is deeply significant to me. It shows our people don’t just want to consume what Africa produces; they want to invest in it, own it, and share in its future. This is the Africa we have always believed in,” he said. “We did not undertake this IPO simply because we needed to raise capital. We wanted to open the doors of ownership, give ordinary Africans an opportunity to participate in an enterprise of global significance and establish a new culture of shared prosperity. We built the refinery in Africa, through African determination, and its future must create opportunities for Africans. “Today, we have made history together. But the greater achievement will be the generation of African investors, entrepreneurs, and industrialists that this transaction inspires. Our ambition is not merely to build successful businesses. It is to help build a prosperous, self-reliant Africa whose people are participants in its economic destiny. As we advance our expansion programme and Vision 2030 strategy, we remain committed to strengthening our operational performance, deepening our contribution to Africa’s energy security and building an enterprise that rewards the confidence placed in it.” The statement said the IPO’s geographical reach is particularly significant for a continent where capital markets have historically been fragmented by national boundaries, differing regulatory environments and limited retail investor participation. By attracting applications from all 54 African countries, the transaction has shown the potential for a more connected investment ecosystem, allowing Africans to participate in major industrial opportunities beyond their domestic markets. The offering also highlights the growing importance of digital financial infrastructure in widening investment access. Through partnerships involving traditional financial institutions and technology-driven investment platforms, the transaction created multiple channels for eligible investors to express interest and submit applications. Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals, David Bird, said the international response reflected confidence in the refinery’s operating capabilities, industrial scale and long-term growth prospects. “The successful conclusion of this IPO is a remarkable milestone for Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals. Investor applications from 120 countries demonstrate extraordinary international interest in our business and the confidence investors place in this refinery’s future. We have built one of the world’s most significant refining and petrochemical complexes, and our focus remains on translating that industrial scale into operational excellence, sustainable growth and long-term shareholder value,” he said. “What makes this transaction particularly meaningful is the breadth of participation. The opportunity to own a stake in a major African industrial enterprise has reached investors across every African country and all six inhabited continents. That is a powerful endorsement of the refinery’s potential and of Africa’s growing relevance in global investment markets.” The refinery’s IPO opened on 14 September, offering 4.1 billion ordinary shares at N525 per share, representing a proposed capital raise of approximately N2.15 trillion. Initially scheduled to close on 13 October, the offer was extended to 27 October after the Securities and Exchange Commission approved it, giving investors across Africa and other international markets more time to participate. The extension reflected the Group’s stated ambition to prioritise broad ownership alongside the transaction’s financial objectives. Beyond the refinery’s industrial significance, the IPO also established a model for collaboration across Africa’s financial services ecosystem. Its distribution network brought together institutions across banking, securities trading, financial technology, and investor engagement, showing how coordinated infrastructure can expand access to large-scale investment opportunities. Dangote Industries Limited Group Chief Financial Officer Murat Erden said the transaction set an important precedent for the continent’s capital markets, speaking to the offering’s execution and broader significance. “The Dangote Refinery People’s IPO represents much more than a landmark capital-raising exercise. It marks a defining moment in the evolution of African capital markets, demonstrating our continent’s ability to mobilise domestic savings, connect investors across borders and broaden ownership of strategic industrial assets. Reaching investors in 120 countries, including all 54 African nations, is an extraordinary achievement and a powerful testament to the continent’s growing appetite for investment. By bringing together banks, capital market institutions, stockbrokers, fintech platforms and innovative digital distribution channels, we have demonstrated that African capital markets can transcend national boundaries and connect millions of people to investment opportunities previously beyond their reach,” he said. “Importantly, this transaction is underpinned by exceptional industrial and financial fundamentals. With US$22.5 billion in revenue and US$5.52 billion in EBITDA in the first nine months of 2026, Dangote Refinery combines world-class industrial scale, strong profitability and significant long-term growth potential. Our greatest achievement is not simply the capital we mobilise, but the doors we open and the foundation we lay for future generations of African investors, entrepreneurs and businesses. We believe the People’s IPO will be remembered not only as a landmark transaction in African capital market history, but also as a blueprint for a more inclusive, interconnected and globally competitive African financial ecosystem — one in which Africans increasingly finance, own and share in the prosperity created by their continent’s industrial transformation.” The successful conclusion of the offer comes as Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals pursues an ambitious programme to expand its refining and petrochemical operations, strengthen its distribution network and support greater energy security across Africa. Located in Lagos, the refinery represents one of the continent’s largest private industrial investments and a major effort to reduce dependence on imported refined petroleum products while building domestic processing capacity

https://www.premiumtimesng.com/business/.body_zh: 丹格特炼油与石化公司已成功完成其具有里程碑意义的首次公开募股（IPO），吸引了来自六大有人居住洲120个国家的投资者申购申请，其中包括非洲全部54个国家。该公司周二发表声明称，这一进展前所未有地展现了非洲大陆调动资本、扩大战略工业资产所有权覆盖范围的能力。此次历史性发行被广泛称为“人民IPO”，实现了对非洲100%的地域覆盖，将非洲各地乃至海外投资者汇聚到一起完成交易，可能重新定义非洲资本市场的规模、可及性和国际影响力。这次IPO不只是传统的融资活动，更成为金融普惠的里程碑，展示了数字技术、协同配合的金融机构以及创新分销渠道如何将数百万潜在投资者与过去主要由机构投资者和高净值人士主导的投资机会连接起来。此次交易得到了广泛商业银行、证券经纪公司、金融科技平台、资本市场机构和分销合作伙伴网络的支持，各方协作突破了国界限制、扩大了本次发行的参与范围，并为散户参与开辟了新路径。对丹格特集团有限公司而言，IPO的完成标志着其工业发展历程中的决定性时刻，使该炼油厂的所有权模式从依靠单一企业家愿景推动的投资，转变为更广泛的非洲投资者共同参与的机会。丹格特集团有限公司总裁兼首席执行官阿里科·丹格特表示，这一成果有力印证了非洲的信心、进取精神以及调动自身资源推动发展的能力。“当初我们着手建设这座炼油厂时，许多人怀疑如此规模的项目能否由非洲人建成。我们证明了非洲能够建设它。如今，通过这次历史性IPO，我们展示了一项同样重要的事实：非洲人已经准备好拥有并参与自身产业所创造的繁荣。“来自非洲全部54个国家的投资者提交申购申请，对我而言意义重大。这表明我们的人民不只想消费非洲生产的产品，还愿意投资并拥有这些产业，分享其未来。这就是我们始终坚信的非洲。”他说。“我们推动这次IPO并非仅仅因为需要筹集资本。我们希望打开所有权的大门，让普通非洲人有机会参与一家具有全球意义的企业，并建立一种共享繁荣的新文化。我们依靠非洲人的决心在非洲建设了这座炼油厂，它的未来也必须为非洲人创造机会。“今天，我们共同创造了历史。但更大的成就，将是这次交易激励起来的非洲投资者、创业者和实业家群体。我们的目标不只是打造成功的企业，还要帮助建设一个繁荣、自给自足的非洲，使非洲人民成为其经济命运的参与者。随着我们推进扩张计划和“2030愿景”战略，我们将继续专注于提升运营表现，深化对非洲能源安全的贡献，并打造一家能够回报投资者信任的企业。”声明称，这次IPO的地域覆盖范围尤其重要，因为非洲大陆的资本市场历来受到国界分割、监管环境差异以及散户参与度有限等因素影响。通过吸引非洲全部54个国家提交申购申请，此次交易展示了一个更加互联的投资生态所具有的潜力，使非洲人能够参与本国市场之外的重要工业投资机会。此次发行还凸显了数字金融基础设施在扩大投资可及性方面日益重要的作用。通过传统金融机构与技术驱动型投资平台之间的合作，此次交易为符合条件的投资者提供了多种表达投资意愿并提交申购申请的渠道。丹格特炼油与石化公司董事总经理兼首席执行官戴维·伯德表示，国际市场反响反映出投资者对该炼油厂运营能力、工业规模及长期增长前景的信心。“这次IPO成功完成，是丹格特炼油与石化公司的重要里程碑。来自120个国家的投资者申购申请证明，国际社会对我们的业务展现出非凡兴趣，也体现了投资者对这家炼油厂未来的信心。我们已经建成全球最具规模的炼油与石化综合体之一，当前重点仍是将这种工业规模转化为卓越运营、可持续增长和长期股东价值。”他说。“让此次交易更具意义的是广泛参与。投资者遍布非洲每一个国家以及六大有人居住洲，并有机会持有一家重要非洲工业企业的股份。这是对该炼油厂潜力以及非洲在全球投资市场中日益提升重要性的有力背书。”该炼油厂的IPO于9月14日开放认购，以每股525奈拉的价格发行41亿股普通股，拟募集资金约2.15万亿奈拉。此次发行原定于10月13日结束，但在证券交易委员会批准后延长至10月27日，为非洲及其他国际市场的投资者提供了更多参与时间。延长期限体现了集团在追求交易财务目标的同时，优先推动广泛所有权的既定愿景。除炼油厂本身的重要工业意义外，此次IPO还为非洲金融服务生态体系内的协作建立了范例。其分销网络将银行、证券交易、金融科技和投资者互动等领域的机构汇聚起来，展示了协同基础设施如何扩大公众参与大规模投资机会。丹格特集团有限公司首席财务官穆拉特·尔登表示，这次交易为非洲大陆资本市场树立了重要先例，其执行过程和广泛意义同样值得关注。“丹格特炼油厂人民IPO远不只是一次具有里程碑意义的融资活动。它标志着非洲资本市场演进过程中的决定性时刻，展现了我们大陆调动国内储蓄、连接跨境投资者以及扩大战略工业资产所有权覆盖范围的能力。投资者覆盖120个国家，包括非洲全部54个国家，这是一项非凡成就，也是非洲大陆投资意愿日益增强的有力证明。通过汇聚银行、资本市场机构、证券经纪商、金融科技平台和创新的数字分销渠道，我们证明了非洲资本市场能够跨越国界，让数百万人获得过去难以触及的投资机会。”他说。“尤为重要的是，这次交易建立在卓越的工业和财务基本面之上。2026年前九个月，丹格特炼油厂实现225亿美元收入和55.2亿美元EBITDA，兼具世界级工业规模、强劲盈利能力及显著的长期增长潜力。我们最大的成就不仅是调动资本，更是打开大门，为未来几代非洲投资者、创业者和企业奠定基础。我们相信，人民IPO不仅会作为非洲资本市场史上的里程碑交易被铭记，也将成为建设更具包容性、更互联且具备全球竞争力的非洲金融生态的蓝图。在这个生态中，非洲人将越来越多地为自身大陆的工业转型提供资金、拥有产业，并分享其创造的繁荣。”此次发行成功完成之际，丹格特炼油与石化公司正推进一项雄心勃勃的计划，以扩大炼油和石化业务、加强分销网络，并支持提升非洲整体能源安全。该炼油厂位于拉各斯，是非洲大陆规模最大的私人工业投资之一，也是非洲为减少对进口成品油依赖、建设本土加工能力所作的重大努力。

https://www.myjoyonline.com/telecel-ghan.body: Senior Manager in charge of Mobile Data at Telecel Ghana, Carlos Asare Oppong, says the promotion reflects the company's commitment to creating rewarding experiences and helping customers achieve their dreams. He disclosed that the latest presentation marks the eighth car awarded under the promotion, in addition to six houses given to winners over the programme's 15 cycles. “We believe that Ghanaians are very aspirational, and as an aspirational brand, we want to be able to support our customers to achieve their dreams and their goals in life. That is why we launched the Dream Car promotion about 15 cycles ago,” he said. Mr Asare Oppong also announced improvements to the 16th cycle of the promotion, including an additional GH¢100,000 cash prize expected to be awarded towards the end of November or December. Meanwhile, winner Eric Ayamgash expressed excitement and gratitude to Telecel Ghana, describing his win as a testament to the authenticity of the promotion. He said after failing to win in the previous year's edition, he was determined to put in more effort in the subsequent cycle. “Last year, I tried but I couldn't win. When I saw the video of the winner, I said to myself that the next one I'm going to try and put in more effort. God being so good, I was called that I am the winner for this cycle. I just want to say thank you very much, Telecel. I'm so grateful,” he said

https://www.myjoyonline.com/ghanaian-mus.summary: Ghanaian Afrobeats and Highlife singer-songwriter King Promise says his ambition is to take Ghanaian music to the global stage without losing the sound and identity that distinguish local artistes from their international counterparts. https://www.myjoyonline.com/ghanaian-mus.summary_zh: 加纳Afrobeats和Highlife创作歌手King Promise表示，他的目标是让加纳音乐走向全球，同时不失去本地艺人与国际同行相区分的声音和身份。这位《Terminator》热门歌曲的创作者称，他此前曾尝试创作深受外国音乐影响的歌曲，但最终意识到，加纳艺人应当发挥自身独特优势，而不是模仿其他地方已经存在的东西。
https://www.myjoyonline.com/ghanaian-mus.body: Ghanaian Afrobeats and Highlife singer-songwriter King Promise says his ambition is to take Ghanaian music to the global stage without losing the sound and identity that distinguish local artistes from their international counterparts. The Terminator hitmaker said he had previously experimented with music heavily influenced by foreign sounds but eventually realised that Ghanaian artistes should build on their unique strengths rather than imitate what already exists elsewhere. Speaking on Joy FM’s Drive Time with Lexis Bill on Tuesday, October 27, he said his focus had always been on achieving global success while maintaining a strong connection with Ghanaian audiences. “I'd rather them not influencing me so much, rather me influencing the world so much,” he said, referring to the influence of international music on his creative direction. King Promise admitted that there was a period when he was making music driven largely by foreign influences, but he chose not to release those experimental songs. “I was making music that was mainly driven by a lot of foreign influence down home, but that was when I was experimenting. I didn't drop them,” he explained. He said he subsequently recognised that Ghanaian musicians possessed distinctive musical qualities that could appeal to international audiences. “What they lack in the rest of the world is what we have here. So why would you trade what you have here for what they have?” he asked. According to him, international success should not require Ghanaian artistes to abandon their musical identity in an attempt to appeal to foreign markets. He cited the global popularity of Spanish-language hit Despacito as an example of how music can cross borders without abandoning its original identity. “If Despacito could be a big record in Ghana, why can't "Mene medofa ahye dam mu" be big in Spain? Or why can't "Terminator" be played in Singapore?” he said. The singer added that his belief in his music and its potential audience had remained central to his career. “It's going to work. It has to work. If it doesn't go this way, we keep going until it goes,” he said. King Promise also discussed the challenge of balancing the tastes of audiences in Ghana with those of listeners abroad. He said he had spent years trying to find a sound that could connect with both markets. He cited songs including Perfect Combi , Paris and Terminator as examples of his efforts to create music with appeal at home and internationally. He also referenced earlier releases such as Tokyo . The singer said he had drawn inspiration from R2Bees, whom he admired while he was in school because of their ability to achieve success both in Ghana and among audiences in the diaspora. He also acknowledged the influence of Nigerian artistes Mr Eazi, Wizkid and Davido, saying their achievements had reinforced his belief that Ghanaian musicians could compete globally. King Promise, who won the Artiste of the Year award, said his international ambitions extended beyond music releases to collaborations and partnerships, including his work with Chelsea Football Club. He maintained that the goal was to help Ghanaian music reach wider audiences while retaining the qualities that make it distinctive
https://www.myjoyonline.com/ghanaian-mus.title_zh: 加纳音乐无需模仿外国音乐风格也能走向全球
https://www.myjoyonline.com/ghanaian-mus.body_zh: 加纳 Afrobeats 和 Highlife 创作歌手 King Promise 表示，他的目标是让加纳音乐走向全球舞台，同时保留让本地艺人区别于国际同行的声音与特色。这位《Terminator》热门歌曲的创作者说，他此前曾尝试创作深受外国音乐影响的歌曲，但后来意识到，加纳艺人应当以自身独特优势为基础，而不是模仿其他地方已有的音乐。周二10月27日，他在 Joy FM 的《Drive Time》节目中与主持人 Lexis Bill 交谈时表示，他始终专注于实现全球成功，同时与加纳听众保持紧密联系。他说：“我宁愿他们没有在那么多方面影响我，而是由我在如此大的程度上影响世界。”他谈的是国际音乐对其创作方向的影响。King Promise 承认，曾有一段时间，他的音乐主要受到外国 influences 驱动，但他选择不发行那些实验性歌曲。他解释道：“那时我创作的音乐主要受到大量外国影响，主要是在国内，但那时我只是在进行探索。我没有发行那些歌曲。”他说，后来他认识到，加纳音乐人拥有能够吸引国际听众的独特音乐特质。他问道：“其他地方所缺乏的，正是我们这里拥有的。那么，你为什么要拿我们这里拥有的东西，去换取他们拥有的东西？”据他所说，国际成功不应要求加纳艺人为了迎合外国市场而放弃自身的音乐身份。他以西语热门歌曲《Despacito》在全球的流行度为例，说明音乐可以在跨越国界的同时保留原有特色。他说：“如果《Despacito》能在加纳成为大热歌曲，为什么《Mene medofa ahye dam mu》不能在西班牙走红？或者，为什么《Terminator》不能在新加坡播放？”这位歌手补充说，他对自己音乐及其潜在受众的信心始终是其职业生涯的核心。“它会奏效的。它一定会奏效。如果这次没有成功，我们就继续前进，直到它成功为止。”King Promise 还讨论了平衡加纳听众与海外听众审美趣味的挑战。他说，多年来他一直试图找到一种能够同时连接两个市场的声音。他以《Perfect Combi》、《Paris》和《Terminator》等歌曲为例，说明自己为创作兼具本土与国际吸引力的音乐所作的努力。他还提到了《Tokyo》等早期作品。这位歌手表示，他在校期间便十分欣赏 R2Bees，并从他们身上获得启发，因为 R2Bees 能够在加纳及海外侨民听众中取得成功。他还承认了尼日利亚艺人 Mr Eazi、Wizkid 和 Davido 的影响，称他们的成就进一步增强了他对加纳音乐人能够在全球竞争的信念。King Promise 曾获得年度艺人奖。他说，自己的国际抱负不仅体现在发行音乐方面，也体现在合作与伙伴关系上，包括与 Chelsea Football Club 的合作。他坚持认为，其目标是帮助加纳音乐触及更广泛的听众，同时保留使其独具特色的品质

https://www.myjoyonline.com/i-compete-wi.title: I compete with myself, not other artistes
https://www.myjoyonline.com/i-compete-wi.summary: Ghanaian Afrobeats and Highlife singer-songwriter Gregory Bortey Newman, known popularly as King Promise, says he is more focused on improving his own achievements than competing with fellow artistes, describing his approach to the music industry as a continuous pursuit of personal growth. King Promise acknowledged that fans often compared artistes and sought to position their favourites against one another, particularly when awards and career achievements were involved.
https://www.myjoyonline.com/i-compete-wi.summary_zh: 加纳Afrobeats和Highlife创作歌手Gregory Bortey Newman（广为人知的艺名为King Promise）表示，比起与同行艺人竞争，他更专注于提升自己的成就，并将自己对待音乐行业的方式描述为持续追求个人成长。King Promise承认，粉丝经常比较各位艺人，试图将自己喜爱的艺人与他人一较高下，尤其是在涉及奖项和职业成就时。
https://www.myjoyonline.com/i-compete-wi.body: Ghanaian Afrobeats and Highlife singer-songwriter Gregory Bortey Newman, known popularly as King Promise, says he is more focused on improving his own achievements than competing with fellow artistes, describing his approach to the music industry as a continuous pursuit of personal growth. The singer said although competition was a normal part of the music business, comparisons between musicians were often driven by fans rather than the artistes themselves. Speaking on Joy FM’s Drive Time with Lexis Bill on Tuesday, October 27, he said his priority was to build on every milestone in his career rather than become preoccupied with the achievements of others. “I've never been but with myself. I'm in my own lane,” he said when asked whether he competed with other musicians. King Promise acknowledged that fans often compared artistes and sought to position their favourites against one another, particularly when awards and career achievements were involved. “It's normal, you know, I believe like when you're in contention to be at the apex of your career, and people are doing similar stuff, it might not even be the artists, it might be the fans that will put you against each other,” he said. He added that he preferred to use the achievements of other musicians as motivation rather than allow comparisons to create resentment. “Rather than have it feel like negative competition, if there's anything that I feel the need to compete is to see someone do something like, ‘Oh, this is nice,’ and I like this. It should inspire me rather than put spite in me,” he explained. The musician cited his relationship with Mr Eazi as an example of how another artiste's success could motivate him. He said watching his friend achieve international recognition had strengthened his belief in what was possible for Ghanaian musicians. King Promise also referred to Wizkid's achievement of selling out London’s O2 Arena, saying it inspired him to pursue similar milestones. “You see Wizkid do something like, ‘Ah bro, he sold out the O2, I want to do it too one day.’ Why was it him and it's not me? That's my mentality,” he said. He explained that his ambition was to keep identifying new levels to reach, regardless of what he had already accomplished. “I'm like, okay, what can we do next? Well, okay, this went this way, I've seen that, okay, it has to go this way next, and that's really what it is,” he said. The singer also spoke about his friendship with Mr Eazi, whom he has known since around 2012, before either of them had a hit song. According to King Promise, their relationship developed from genuine friendship rather than a deliberate effort to collaborate musically. He said Mr Eazi had influenced him through his directness, confidence and business-minded approach, adding that the two often exchanged ideas beyond music. King Promise said he valued relationships built on genuine connections, citing his longstanding associations with Mr Eazi, R2Bees and Sarkodie. Looking ahead, he told Lexis Bill that he had major plans for his career in Ghana and internationally. He also mentioned new music, future music videos, an upcoming album and his Promise Land event as part of his plans. He further hinted that he might release another song before the end of the year, although he did not confirm a date
https://www.myjoyonline.com/i-compete-wi.title_zh: 我与自己竞争，而不是与其他艺人竞争
https://www.myjoyonline.com/i-compete-wi.body_zh: 加纳Afrobeats及Highlife创作歌手格雷戈里·博尔特·纽曼（广为人知艺名为King Promise）表示，与其他艺人竞争相比，他更专注于提升自己的成绩，并将自己对待音乐行业的方式视为不断追求个人成长。这名歌手说，尽管竞争是音乐行业的常态，但音乐人之间的比较往往源于粉丝，而非艺人本人。10月27日星期二，他在Joy FM的《Drive Time》节目中接受主持人莱克西斯·比尔的采访时表示，他的重点是在职业生涯的每一个里程碑上继续前进，而不是把心思放在他人的成就上。当被问及是否与其他音乐人竞争时，King Promise说：“我从来只做自己，走自己的路。”King Promise承认，粉丝经常比较各位艺人，试图将自己喜爱的人彼此对标，尤其是在涉及奖项和职业成就时。他说：“你知道，这很正常。我认为，当你在争取把事业推向顶峰，而其他人也在做类似的事情时，把你们彼此放在一起比较的甚至可能不是艺人，而是粉丝。”他补充说，他更愿意把其他音乐人的成就当作动力，而不是让比较滋生怨恨。他解释道：“与其让这种比较变成负面竞争，如果有什么让我觉得需要较劲，那就是看到有人做成某件事，比如，‘哦，这个真不错，我喜欢这个。’这应该启发我，而不是让我心生嫉妒。”这位音乐人以自己与Mr Eazi的关系为例，说明另一位艺人的成功如何激励自己。他说，看到朋友在国际上获得认可，让他更加相信加纳音乐人能够取得怎样的成就。King Promise还提到Wizkid售罄伦敦O2 Arena的成就，称这件事激励他追求类似的里程碑。他说：“你看到Wizkid做成某件事，比如，‘啊，兄弟，他售罄了O2，我以后也要做到。’为什么是他而不是我？这就是我的心态。”他解释道，无论自己已经取得了什么成绩，他的抱负都是不断找到新的高度继续攀登。他说：“我会想，好，接下来我们还能做什么？好，这个是这样发展，我已经见过了，那下一步就必须朝那个方向走，这才是真正的想法。”这位歌手还谈到自己与Mr Eazi的友谊；大约从2012年起，在两人任何一人都还没有热门歌曲之前，他就认识Mr Eazi了。据King Promise所说，两人的关系建立在真诚的友谊之上，并非有意为音乐合作而刻意建立。他说，Mr Eazi的直接、自信和商业思维影响了他，两人也经常交流音乐以外的想法。King Promise表示，他重视建立在真诚联系上的关系，并提到自己与Mr Eazi、R2Bees及Sarkodie的长期交情。展望未来，他告诉莱克西斯·比尔，自己对在加纳及国际市场的发展都有重大计划。他还提到，新音乐、未来的音乐录影带、即将发行的专辑以及Promise Land活动均在计划之中。他进一步暗示，自己可能在年底前再发行一首歌，但没有确认具体日期……

https://www.thehindu.com/opinion/lead/in.summary: More consequential, however, was the shift in India’s stance on the United States-Israel war against Iran and Russia’s war in Ukraine. Traditionally, the SCO and BRICS summits have offered the three major powers — Russia, India and China — an opportunity to demonstrate their mutual solidarity. Russia is now leaning ever more toward its “trusted partner” — China, while Mr. Modi’s performative diplomacy designed to stay in the good books of Washington risks undermining the long enduring Russia-India friendship.
https://www.thehindu.com/opinion/lead/in.summary_zh: 然而，更具影响的是，印度对美国和以色列对伊朗的战争以及俄罗斯对乌克兰的战争所持立场的转变。传统上，上合组织和金砖国家峰会一直为俄罗斯、印度和中国这三个大国提供了展示相互团结的机会。如今，俄罗斯越来越向其“可信伙伴”中国靠拢，而莫迪先生为讨好华盛顿而进行的表演式外交，可能损害俄罗斯与印度长期持久的友谊。
https://www.thehindu.com/opinion/lead/in.body: Account subscription benefits alongside Premium Stories, Editorials, Opinions and more. Unlock these with Subscription The Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, on August 31-September 1, 2026, and the BRICS summit in New Delhi on September 12-13, 2026, were remarkable. Iran received considerably more attention and support from members of both the groups, far more than anticipated. More consequential, however, was the shift in India’s stance on the United States-Israel war against Iran and Russia’s war in Ukraine. Traditionally, the SCO and BRICS summits have offered the three major powers — Russia, India and China — an opportunity to demonstrate their mutual solidarity. For Russia, it is a platform from which it can signal to the West that it is not isolated and still has powerful allies. The expansion of the SCO and BRICS under China’s leadership showcases its growing power to the West. For India, the SCO and BRICS have been useful for demonstrating its strategic autonomy. India has sought to remain welcome in both western and non-western forums, from the G-7 to the SCO and BRICS. At Bishkek, however, India sprang two surprises. First, it endorsed the Bishkek Declaration, which condemned the attacks on Iran as violations of international law, reaffirmed Iran’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, and mourned the killing of its Supreme Leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, in U.S.-Israeli air strikes on February 28, 2026. PM Modi, Vladimir Putin direct officials to expand cooperation, target $100 bn trade by 2030: Envoy India is discussing agreements on grains and maritime safety with Moscow and Kyiv: Jaishankar PM Modi has ‘good ideas’ for settlement of Ukraine conflict: Putin Russia welcomes India’s contribution to end Ukraine crisis: Kremlin spokesperson India in continuous touch with Ukraine and Russia to help end the conflict: Jaishankar Although the declaration did not name the U.S. or Israel, its meaning was unmistakable. India reaffirmed its opposition to military strikes on Iran by endorsing the Bishkek Declaration, which condemned the attacks and reiterated support for Iran’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. Second, Prime Minister Narendra Modi made an unusually blunt appeal to Russian President Vladimir Putin to bring Russia’s seemingly endless war in Ukraine to an end. India has generally sought to avoid directly condemning the U.S. or Israel for their military actions against Iran, even though Iran, like India, is a member of both the SCO and BRICS. India had previously avoided explicitly accusing Israel of genocide in Gaza, although it had supported UN resolutions calling for a ceasefire and reaffirmed its commitment to Palestinian statehood. Indeed, New Delhi had emphatically declared that it stands with Israel, while often working in multilateral forums to soften language that is critical of Washington and Tel Aviv. But in both the Bishkek and Delhi Declarations, India signed on to very strong criticism of Israel as well as very strong affirmation of Palestinian rights and the two-state solution. One interpretation of this pivot in policy is that India may have signed on to the declaration to avoid alienating Mr. Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping, and thereby jeopardising their attendance at India’s BRICS summit. Without the two leaders, India’s presidency of BRICS this year would have been a complete failure. Since Operation Sindoor (2025), India has faced a growing perception of diplomatic marginalisation. Meanwhile, Pakistan has gained diplomatic prominence through Washington’s selection of Islamabad as a mediator in the conflict with Iran, while several Gulf nations have sought defence agreements with Pakistan. Consequently, India needed a successful and high-profile BRICS summit, which it got. While there is a shift in India’s policy, New Delhi has not abandoned Washington entirely. Mr. Modi’s public appeal to Mr. Putin to end the endless war in Ukraine can therefore be read as a counter-signal to Washington. Had the message been intended only for Moscow, it could have been conveyed privately. Delivering it publicly suggested that Mr. Modi was also reassuring the West. India may have joined the SCO and BRICS consensus on Iran to secure a successful BRICS summit, but it was now leaning more toward the western position on Ukraine than before. India among Russia's top foreign trade partners: PM Mishustin These apparently contradictory shifts reveal the strain on India’s foreign policy. New Delhi wants to support Israel while condemning attacks on Iran; buy Russian oil while aligning more closely with the West on Ukraine; and remain central to BRICS and the SCO while assuring Washington that it is not part of an anti-American bloc. Multi-alignment is becoming an increasingly difficult exercise in this era of change and turbulence. India’s balancing act is unlikely to sit comfortably with either Moscow or Beijing. Although Mr. Modi and Mr. Xi did not meet bilaterally at the SCO summit in Bishkek, they held talks on the sidelines of the BRICS summit in New Delhi. The meeting preceded Mr. Xi’s high-profile G2 summit with U.S. President Donald Trump in Washington, which was held in September 2026. Neither summit declaration mentioned the war in Ukraine, avoiding criticism of Moscow even as Mr. Modi publicly urged Mr. Putin to end the conflict. India thus endorsed two declarations accommodating Russia’s position without fully embracing it. From Mr. Putin’s perspective, this was the second time that Mr. Modi had used what might be called ‘jumla’ (performative) diplomacy at Russia’s expense. At Samarkand on September 16, 2022, Mr. Modi told Mr. Putin that “today’s era is not an era of war”. External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar subsequently repeated that phrase in western capitals to demonstrate that India’s purchase of discounted Russian oil did not signify political support for Russia’s invasion. The selectivity of these admonitions is difficult to ignore. Mr. Modi has not used comparable language toward Mr. Netanyahu, even as Israel has attacked several countries and territories across West Asia, many on multiple occasions, and has committed genocide in Gaza. Nor has Mr. Modi publicly directed the same admonition at Mr. Trump following American attacks on Iran. India itself attacked Pakistan during Operation Sindoor. Mr. Putin may therefore conclude that Mr. Modi’s declaration that this is “not an era of war” reflects neither a consistent principle nor a universal opposition to war, but diplomatic messaging designed to reassure the West at Russia’s expense. Mr. Modi’s latest appeal — that “endless war” must give way to an “end of war” — may reinforce that perception. Would Mr. Modi deliver the same message to Mr. Trump about the increasingly prolonged war with Iran — or to Mr. Netanyahu about his unending campaign of revenge in Gaza? How is Moscow interpreting this double standard? Russia, nevertheless, still needs India, at least for now, as a major purchaser of its oil and military equipment. At the same time, Moscow can see that New Delhi has steadily reduced its dependence on Russian arms by turning increasingly to France, Israel, and the U.S. The relationship remains important to both countries, but it is becoming increasingly transactional — and vulnerable to their diverging strategic priorities. Russia is now leaning ever more toward its “trusted partner” — China, while Mr. Modi’s performative diplomacy designed to stay in the good books of Washington risks undermining the long enduring Russia-India friendship. Muqtedar Khan is Professor of International Relations at the University of Delaware and a Senior Non-Resident Fellow of the Middle East Policy Council. 2026年8月31日至9月1日在吉尔吉斯斯坦比什凯克举行的上海合作组织（SCO）峰会，以及2026年9月12日至13日在新德里举行的金砖国家峰会，都引人瞩目。伊朗在这两大组织的成员国中获得了远超预期的关注和支持。然而，更具影响意义的是，印度对美以战争针对伊朗以及俄罗斯在乌克兰的战争所持立场的转变。

传统上，SCO和金砖国家峰会为俄罗斯、印度和中国这三大国提供了展示相互团结的机会。对俄罗斯而言，这是一个向西方表明自身并未陷入孤立、仍拥有强大盟友的平台。中国领导下的SCO和金砖国家扩张，展示了其日益增强的力量，令西方不得不正视。对印度而言，SCO和金砖国家有助于展示其战略自主。印度一直寻求在西方和非西方论坛中都受到欢迎，从G-7到SCO和金砖国家均是如此。

然而，在比什凯克，印度出人意料地采取了两项行动。第一，印度支持了《比什凯克宣言》。该宣言谴责针对伊朗的袭击违反国际法，重申伊朗的主权和领土完整，并对最高领袖阿里·哈梅内伊在2026年2月28日遭美以空袭身亡表示哀悼。

印度总理莫迪指示官员扩大合作，目标到2030年实现1000亿美元贸易额：特使

印度正与莫斯科和基辅讨论粮食及海上安全协议：沙希坎特

印度总理莫迪对解决乌克兰冲突有“好主意”：普京

俄罗斯欢迎印度为结束乌克兰危机作出的贡献：克里姆林宫发言人

印度持续与乌克兰和俄罗斯保持联系，以帮助结束冲突：沙希坎特

尽管宣言没有点名美国或以色列，但其含义毋庸置疑。印度通过支持《比什凯克宣言》，重申反对针对伊朗的军事打击；该宣言谴责相关袭击，并再次支持伊朗的主权和领土完整。

第二，印度总理纳伦德拉·莫迪异常直率地呼吁俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京，让俄罗斯在乌克兰似乎永无止境的战争尽快结束。印度通常避免直接谴责美国或以色列针对伊朗的军事行动，尽管伊朗与印度一样，也是SCO和金砖国家成员。此前，印度一直避免明确指责以色列在加沙实施种族灭绝，尽管它支持要求停火的联合国决议，并重申对巴勒斯坦建国目标的承诺。事实上，新德里曾斩钉截铁地宣称与以色列站在一起，同时又经常在多边论坛中推动措辞软化，以免对华盛顿和特拉维夫形成过于尖锐的批评。

但无论在《比什凯克宣言》还是《德里宣言》中，印度都签署了对以色列的强烈批评，同时强烈确认巴勒斯坦权利和两国方案。

对这一政策转向的一种解读是，印度签署宣言或许是为了避免疏远普京先生和中国国家主席习近平，从而避免危及二人出席印度主办的金砖国家峰会。若两位领导人缺席，印度今年担任金砖国家轮值主席国将彻底失败。自“辛杜尔行动”（2025年）以来，印度越来越感受到自己在外交上被边缘化。与此同时，随着华盛顿选择伊斯兰堡充当与伊朗冲突的调解方，巴基斯坦的外交影响力有所提升；多个海湾国家也寻求与巴基斯坦签署防务协议。因此，印度需要一场成功且备受瞩目的金砖国家峰会，而它确实实现了这一目标。

尽管印度政策有所转变，新德里并未完全抛弃华盛顿。因此，莫迪先生公开呼吁普京先生结束乌克兰无休止的战争，也可以被理解为向华盛顿发出的反向信号。如果这一信息只打算传给莫斯科，完全可以私下传达。公开传达则表明，莫迪先生也在安抚西方。

印度可能为了确保金砖国家峰会取得成功而加入了SCO和金砖国家有关伊朗的共识，但现在在乌克兰问题上，它比以往更倾向西方的立场。

印度是俄罗斯主要对外贸易伙伴之一：米舒斯京总理

这些看似矛盾的立场变化，揭示了印度外交政策承受的压力。新德里希望一方面支持以色列并谴责针对伊朗的袭击，另一方面购买俄罗斯石油并在与西方关于乌克兰问题上的立场上更加靠拢；同时，它既要在金砖国家和SCO中占据核心地位，又要向华盛顿保证自己并非反美集团的一员。在这个变化与动荡的时代，多重结盟正变得越来越难以驾驭。印度的平衡策略无论对莫斯科还是北京而言，都不太可能令人安心。

尽管莫迪先生和习近平主席未在比什凯克举行的SCO峰会上举行双边会晤，但二人在新德里金砖国家峰会期间进行了会谈。这次会谈发生在习近平主席于2026年9月在华盛顿与美国总统唐纳德·特朗普举行备受瞩目的G2峰会之前。两份峰会宣言均未提及乌克兰战争，从而避免了对莫斯科的批评，尽管莫迪先生公开敦促普京先生结束冲突。因此，印度支持了两份既照顾俄罗斯立场、又没有完全接受该立场的宣言。

从普京先生的角度看，这是莫迪先生第二次以牺牲俄罗斯为代价，利用所谓的“乔姆拉”（表演式）外交。2022年9月16日在撒马尔罕，莫迪先生告诉普京先生：“当今时代不是战争的时代。”此后，外交部长S.沙希坎特在西方各国首都重复了这句话，以表明印度购买打折俄罗斯石油并不意味着在政治上支持俄罗斯入侵乌克兰。

这些告诫的选择性很难不引人注意。莫迪先生并未对内塔尼亚胡先生使用类似措辞，尽管以色列袭击了西亚多个国家和地区，其中许多还遭到不止一次袭击，并且已在加沙犯下种族灭绝罪行。美国袭击伊朗后，莫迪先生也未公开向特朗普先生提出同样的告诫。印度自身在“辛杜尔行动”中袭击了巴基斯坦。

因此，普京先生或许会得出结论：莫迪先生宣称“这是不是一个战争的时代”，既不反映一贯原则，也不代表对战争的普遍反对，而是一种旨在牺牲俄罗斯来安抚西方的外交信息。

莫迪先生最新提出的呼吁——让“无休止的战争”让位于“战争的终结”——可能会进一步加深这种印象。对于与伊朗之间日益持久的战争，莫迪先生会向特朗普先生传达同样的信息吗？对于内塔尼亚胡先生在加沙永无止境的复仇行动，他又会传达同样的信息吗？莫斯科如何解读这种双重标准？

不过，至少目前俄罗斯仍需要印度，因为印度是其石油和军事装备的主要购买方。与此同时，莫斯科也能看到，新德里正通过越来越多地转向法国、以色列和美国，逐步减少对俄罗斯武器的依赖。俄印关系对两国仍然重要，但正日益变成一种交易性关系，也更容易因双方战略重点的分歧而受损。

俄罗斯如今越来越向其“可信伙伴”中国靠拢，而莫迪先生为博取华盛顿好感而采取的表演式外交，可能损害俄罗斯与印度长久的友谊。

The w3 Awards recognise excellence in digital creativity, content and online experiences.
