https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/economy/202.summary: Korean stocks traded higher late Tuesday morning, led by gains in technology shares, as renewed optimism over artificial intelligence (AI) and falling oil prices boosted risk appetite.
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/economy/202.summary_zh: 周二上午晚些时候，韩国股市走高，科技股领涨。随着市场对人工智能的乐观情绪重燃以及油价下跌，风险偏好得到提振。
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/economy/202.body: Korean stocks traded higher late Tuesday morning, led by gains in technology shares, as renewed optimism over artificial intelligence (AI) and falling oil prices boosted risk appetite. After opening 3.46 percent higher, the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) extended its earlier gains to trade up 213.1 points, or 3.9 percent, to 5,682.6 as of 11:20 a.m. Amid a rally driven by foreign buying, the Korea Exchange activated a buy-side sidecar at 10:13 a.m., suspending buy orders in program trading for KOSPI-listed shares for five minutes. The measure is triggered when KOSPI 200 futures rise at least 5 percent and remain at that level for one minute or longer. Overnight, the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 0.28 percent, while the S&P 500 advanced 0.7 percent and the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite climbed 0.82 percent. Investor sentiment improved after AI startup Anthropic disclosed strong revenue growth in its U.S. initial public offering (IPO) filing, reigniting enthusiasm for AI-related stocks ahead of major tech earnings and the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision. Oil prices also retreated on hopes of easing tensions in the Middle East, following reports of Qatari mediation efforts involving Iran and the United States. Market bellwether Samsung Electronics gained 4.69 percent, and chip giant SK hynix increased 6.59 percent. SK Square, the parent firm of SK hynix, jumped 10.79 percent, and Samsung Electro-Mechanics, an electronics component affiliate of Samsung Electronics, surged 7.78 percent. The Korean won was trading at 1,323.2 won against the U.S. dollar at 11:20 a.m., up 2.8 won from the close of the previous stock trading session
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/economy/202.title_zh: 受华尔街股市上涨和人工智能乐观情绪提振，首尔股市开盘走高
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/economy/202.body_zh: 韩国股市周二上午晚盘走高，科技股领涨，人工智能（AI）乐观情绪重燃、油价下跌提振了风险偏好。基准韩国综合股价指数（KOSPI）开盘上涨3.46%，随后延续早盘涨幅，截至上午11时20分上涨213.1点，涨幅3.9%，报5,682.6点。在外资买入推动的涨势中，韩国交易所于上午10时13分启动买方临时停牌机制，暂停KOSPI上市股票程序化交易的买单5分钟。当KOSPI 200期货涨幅至少达到5%，并在该水平维持1分钟或更长时间时，就会触发这一措施。隔夜，道琼斯工业平均指数上涨0.28%，标普500指数上涨0.7%，以科技股为主的纳斯达克综合指数上涨0.82%。人工智能初创公司Anthropic披露其美国首次公开募股（IPO）申请文件显示营收强劲增长，投资者情绪随之改善；在科技行业主要企业即将公布财报以及美联储即将决定利率之际，人工智能相关股票再次引发投资热情。卡塔尔据报正就伊朗与美国进行斡旋，市场期待中东紧张局势缓解，油价随之回落。市场风向标Samsung Electronics上涨4.69%，芯片巨头SK hynix上涨6.59%。SK hynix母公司SK Square暴涨10.79%，Samsung Electronics旗下电子零部件关联公司Samsung Electro-Mechanics大涨7.78%。截至上午11时20分，韩元兑美元汇价为1,323.2韩元，较上一股票交易日收盘时上涨2.8韩元。

https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/southkorea/.title: 'Doctor X' faces petition to halt airing over Gwangju Uprising depiction
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/southkorea/.summary: Medical drama joins list of disputes over fictional portrayals of Korea's modern history The Korean medical drama “Doctor X: Mafia in White” has become the latest target of political controversy over how fictional works portray history, after a National Assembly petition demanded a halt to its airing over its depiction of the 1980 Gwangju Uprising. The petition, posted Saturday on the National Assembly’s petition website, calls for a review of the drama’s production and a halt to its broadcast.
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/southkorea/.summary_zh: 医疗剧加入围绕韩国现代史虚构描写的争议名单。在国会请愿要求停止播出该剧后，韩国医疗剧《X博士：白衣黑手》成为政治争议的最新目标，争议焦点是虚构作品如何描绘历史；请愿方称该剧对1980年光州起义的描绘存在问题。周六发布在国会请愿网站上的请愿书，要求审查该剧的制作并停止播出。
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/southkorea/.body: Medical drama joins list of disputes over fictional portrayals of Korea's modern history The Korean medical drama “Doctor X: Mafia in White” has become the latest target of political controversy over how fictional works portray history, after a National Assembly petition demanded a halt to its airing over its depiction of the 1980 Gwangju Uprising. The petition, posted Saturday on the National Assembly’s petition website, calls for a review of the drama’s production and a halt to its broadcast. It has gathered the 100 supporters required to be made public. The petitioner said Episode 6, which aired Saturday, depicted the 1980 pro-democracy movement in Gwangju despite its having no connection to the plot. “The uprising remains a political issue, with the ruling and opposition parties and the left and right divided on some aspects,” the petitioner said. “Broadly, no one would dispute that it is a painful chapter of history, but it is hard to accept a drama abruptly using the uprising, which is still politically contested in its details.” The episode featured a character suffering the effects of a gunshot wound to the head sustained during the uprising, along with flashbacks to Gwangju in 1980 and scenes of tear gas and bullets striking ordinary citizens. The Korean series is an adaptation of the Japanese medical drama “Doctor X: Surgeon Michiko Daimon.” The Gwangju Uprising storyline does not appear in the Japanese original and was introduced by the Korean production, making it a deliberate creative choice specific to the local adaptation. Shortly after the episode aired, Lee Ok-kyu, chief producer of the drama, posted its poster on social media with the phrase “no fear,” without elaborating. The pro-democracy movement erupted in the southwestern city of Gwangju in 1980, when citizens stood up against the imposition of martial law extended nationwide by the military junta led by Chun Doo-hwan, who would become president later that year. The crackdown left hundreds dead or missing and it has since been recognized as a pivotal moment in Korea’s long road to democratization, though some in far-right circles denigrate the movement. The controversy is the latest in a string of disputes over fictional portrayals of history. Last month, director Hur Jin-ho’s historical thriller “The Assassin(s)” sparked a growing political dispute and a defamation investigation over its depiction of the 1974 shooting that killed then-first lady Yuk Young-soo. The Gwangju Uprising has also been at the center of controversy, particularly this year, as attempts to insult or ridicule it have emerged despite being long recognized as a pro-democracy movement. On May 18, Starbucks Korea launched a “Tank Day” promotion, using the phrase in a way widely condemned as denigrating the pro-democracy movement. The backlash drew responses from consumers and politicians alike. In June, the Paichai High School baseball team was embroiled in controversy after some players repeatedly chanted “Let’s go, let’s go, let’s go to Starbucks” in unison during a match against Gwangju Jeil High School, evoking the promotion. One even shouted “Tank Day.” False claims about the pro-democracy movement, including assertions that it was a riot or involved North Korean troops, are also common online and continue to circulate among far-right circles. The May 18 Foundation said in May that it found 5,182 posts, comments and videos distorting or denigrating the uprising between February and November last year, up roughly 200 percent from the same period a year earlier. Under a 2021 special act, distorting or defaming the uprising can carry up to five years in prison, though enforcement has been limited. National Police Agency data submitted to Rep. Yang Bu-nam of the Democratic Party of Korea shows that police have booked 120 suspects under the act from 2021 through April this year, with only 67 referred to prosecutors
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/southkorea/.title_zh: “X博士”因对光州起义的描绘面临停止播出的请愿
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/southkorea/.body_zh: 医疗剧因虚构呈现韩国现代史而引发争议。韩国医疗剧《Doctor X：白色黑手党》在因呈现1980年光州起义而受到政治争议后，成为虚构作品如何再现历史这一系列争议的最新目标。国民议会请愿网站周六发布的请愿书要求停止播出该剧，理由是其对1980年光州起义的描绘。该请愿已获得公开所需的100名支持者署名。请愿发起人表示，周六播出的第6集尽管与剧情主线无关，却描绘了1980年光州的民主运动。请愿发起人说：“起义至今仍是一个政治议题，执政党、反对党以及左右翼之间在某些方面存在分歧。总体而言，没有人会否认这是历史上痛苦的一章，但难以接受一部电视剧突然利用这场起义，而起义的诸多细节在政治上仍有争议。”该集出现了一名因起义期间头部中枪而留下后遗症的角色，并以闪回方式呈现1980年的光州，以及催泪瓦斯和子弹袭击普通民众的场景。这部韩国剧集改编自日本医疗剧《Doctor X：大门司未知子》。光州起义的情节并未出现在日本原作中，而是韩国制作方加入的，因此成为本地改编中有意作出的创作选择。该集播出后不久，该剧首席制片人李玉秋在社交媒体上发布了剧海报，并配以“无所畏惧”字样，但未作进一步说明。这场民主运动于1980年在西南部城市光州爆发，当时市民奋起反对军政府将戒严令扩大到全国。军政府由全斗焕领导，他后来于同年成为总统。镇压行动造成数百人死亡或失踪，此后被视为韩国漫长民主化进程中的关键时刻，不过仍有一些极右翼人士贬低这场运动。此次争议是围绕虚构作品再现历史的一连串纠纷中最新的一起。上个月，导演许晋镐的历史惊悚片《The Assassin(s)》因呈现1974年导致时任总统夫人俞良淑遇害的枪击案，引发日益扩大的政治争议和诽谤调查。光州起义也一直是争议焦点，尤其是在今年。尽管该运动长期以来被认定为民主运动，但网络上仍不断出现侮辱或嘲笑它的言论。5月18日，韩国星巴克推出“坦克日”促销，其用语方式受到广泛谴责，被认为是在贬低这场民主运动。消费者的反弹也引起政界人士回应。6月，培才高中棒球队在与光州济一高中比赛的比赛中陷入争议，因为部分球员齐声反复高喊“去吧，去吧，去星巴克”，令人联想到该促销活动，甚至有人喊出“坦克日”。有关这场民主运动的不实说法在网上也很常见，其中包括声称该运动是暴乱或涉及朝鲜军队，这些说法继续在极右翼圈子里流传。5月18日基金会今年5月表示，去年2月至11月间，共发现5,182条歪曲或贬低这场起义的帖子、评论和视频，较上年同期增长约200%。根据2021年颁布的一部特别法，歪曲或诽谤这场起义最高可判处5年监禁，但执法力度有限。提交给韩国民主党议员杨伯南的韩国警察厅数据显示，自2021年至今年4月，警方依据该法已对120名嫌疑人立案，但仅有67人被移送检方

https://www.yna.co.kr/view/akr2026102708.title: 조현 "북중 간 북미대화 관련 논의 가능성 있다고 봐"
https://www.yna.co.kr/view/akr2026102708.summary: (서울=연합뉴스) 김지헌 기자 = 조현 외교부 장관은 지난 24일 북한 국무위원장 김정은의 중국 단둥 방문과 관련, 중국과 북한 간 북미대화와 관련한 논의를 나눴을 가능성이 있다고 봤다. 조 장관은 27일 국회 외교통일위원회 종합국정감사에서 국민의힘 권영세 의원이 마자오쉬 중국 외교부 상무부부장도 단둥에 나타난 점을 들어 가능성을 어떻게 보느냐고 질문하자 "가능성이 있다고 본다"고 말했다. 조 장관은 중국이 김 위원장의 단둥 방문을 사전에 알려주지는 않았다면서 북미대화 논의 가능성에 대해 "아직 단정 짓기 어려운 상황"이라며 "여러 가지 요소들을 함께 고려해야 할 것 같다"고 덧붙였다.
https://www.yna.co.kr/view/akr2026102708.summary_zh: （首尔＝韩联社）记者金智贤报道＝韩国外交部长赵显27日表示，朝鲜国务委员会委员金正恩24日访问中国丹东时，双方很可能讨论了有关朝美对话以及中国与朝鲜之间的关系。在国会外交日内委员会综合国政审计中，共同民主党权永锡议员询问如何看待马朝晖作为中国外交部常务副部长出现在丹东一事，赵显回答称：“我认为存在这种可能性。”赵显还表示，中国事前并未告知他金正恩访问丹东的行程；对于朝美对话讨论的可能性，他称：“目前仍难以断定，看来需要综合考虑多种因素。”
https://www.yna.co.kr/view/akr2026102708.body: (서울=연합뉴스) 김지헌 기자 = 조현 외교부 장관은 지난 24일 북한 국무위원장 김정은의 중국 단둥 방문과 관련, 중국과 북한 간 북미대화와 관련한 논의를 나눴을 가능성이 있다고 봤다. 조 장관은 27일 국회 외교통일위원회 종합국정감사에서 국민의힘 권영세 의원이 마자오쉬 중국 외교부 상무부부장도 단둥에 나타난 점을 들어 가능성을 어떻게 보느냐고 질문하자 "가능성이 있다고 본다"고 말했다. 조 장관은 중국이 김 위원장의 단둥 방문을 사전에 알려주지는 않았다면서 북미대화 논의 가능성에 대해 "아직 단정 짓기 어려운 상황"이라며 "여러 가지 요소들을 함께 고려해야 할 것 같다"고 덧붙였다. 그는 더불어민주당 맹성규 의원이 북한을 다시 대화로 끌어들이기 위한 전략을 묻자 "북미 정상회담이 열리는 것이 현 상황을 타개하는 하나의 기폭제가 되지 않을까 생각한다"고 말했다. 이어 "그걸 기초로 해서 우리가 페이스메이커로 역할을 충실히 해서 미국이 피스메이커로 자리 잡을 수 있도록 노력하는 것이 저의 전략이고, 이를 위해 중국·러시아 등 관련 국가와도 긴밀히 사전 조율을 해나가면서 북한을 테이블로 끌어내는 것이 중요하다"고 덧붙였다. 조 장관은 신압록강대교 개통으로 대북 제재가 약화할 수 있다는 취지의 권 의원 지적에 "그 전부터 제재가 실질적으로 이행되지 않는 데 대한 우려"가 있었다며 "중국이 그래도 대북 제재의 큰 원칙은 훼손하지 않으려고 해왔다"고 말했다. 그러면서 "그런데 북한과 러시아가 밀착하면서 중국도 압박받고, 어떤 형태로든지 북한에 대한 지원을 더 하려고 하는 것으로 보인다"고 분석했다. 제보는 카카오톡 okjebo <저작권자(c) 연합뉴스, 무단 전재-재배포, AI 학습 및 활용 금지> 2026/10/27 11:16 송고 2026년10월27일 11시16분 송고 (서울=연합뉴스) 신현우 기자 = 조현 외교부 장관이 27일 국회 외교통일위원회에서 열린 외교부, 통일부 등에 대한 종합감사에서 외통위원 질의에 답하고 있다. 2026.10.27 nowwego@yna.co.kr
https://www.yna.co.kr/view/akr2026102708.title_zh: 赵显称“韩中之间可能讨论北美韩朝关系问题”
https://www.yna.co.kr/view/akr2026102708.body_zh:
（首尔＝韩联社）记者金智贤报道：外交部长赵显27日就朝鲜国务委员会委员长金正恩访华并前往山东一事表示，有关方面可能就朝美对话以及中朝之间相关问题进行了讨论。当国民力量党议员权永世在国会外交统一委员会综合国政监察会议上询问，朝鲜国务委员会委员长金正恩访问山东以及中国外交部副部长马朝旭也出现在山东一事是否意味着双方曾进行讨论时，赵显回答称：“我认为存在这种可能性。”

赵显表示，中国事前并未告知朝鲜国务委员会委员长访山东一事，但就朝美对话讨论的可能性而言，“目前仍难以作出断定”，并补充称，“似乎还需要综合考虑多种因素。”

当执政党议员朴成圭询问将朝鲜重新拉回对话桌的策略时，赵显说：“我认为，朝美首脑会谈若能举行，或将成为打破当前僵局的一枚引爆点。”

他接着说：“以此为基础，我们忠实履行斡旋者角色，努力让美国能够成为斡旋者，同时继续与中国、俄罗斯等相关国家进行密切的事前协调，把朝鲜拉回谈判桌十分重要。”

针对权永世议员指出新印洛线铁路桥开通可能导致对朝制裁效力减弱一事，赵显表示：“此前就一直担忧制裁未能得到切实执行。”他说：“即便如此，中国一直努力不破坏对朝制裁的重大原则。”

随后他分析称：“然而，随着朝鲜与俄罗斯密切接触，中国也正承受压力，看来正以某种形式加大对朝鲜的支持。”

https://dailytrust.com/nigeria-supplies-.body: Nigeria’s domestic refineries received more than 127 million barrels of Nigerian crude oil and condensate between January and September 2026 as the Federal Government intensifies efforts to strengthen local refining and reduce dependence on imported petroleum products. The Commission Chief Executive of the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC), Mrs. Oritsemeyiwa Eyesan, disclosed this at the 20th anniversary edition of OTL Africa Downstream Energy Week in Lagos on Monday. NUPRC is also consulting producers, refiners and other stakeholders on a domestic crude swap framework. “Under it, a refiner could receive crude from the nearest suitable production or export point instead of moving an allocated grade over long distances, which could take an estimated three to four dollars off the cost of every barrel,” he added. On production, Eyesan said Nigeria recorded an average of 1.717 million barrels per day of crude oil and condensate in September, a 2.34 per cent increase over August. Crude oil production alone averaged 1.53 million barrels per day, marking the fifth consecutive month the industry met or exceeded its quota. She attributed the improvement to better asset integrity, enhanced security of evacuation infrastructure, stronger collaboration with operators and sustained regulatory efforts to restore shut-in production. On the 2026 Licensing Round, she said the 40 blocks on offer would be subjected to a transparent evaluation process, with published criteria and mandatory disclosure of beneficial ownership. The NUPRC boss added that the Commission was enforcing the drill-or-drop principle to discourage speculative holding of licences, noting that 22 recent awardees were expected to contribute at least 250,000 barrels per day within five years. She reaffirmed the Commission’s commitment to meeting the Domestic Gas Delivery Obligation and working with the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA) to align refinery demand with crude supply planning, ensuring that upstream gains translate into tangible benefits for households, industries and power generation. Meanwhile, the Authority Chief Executive of the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA), Engr. Rabiu Abdullahi Umar, said locally refined petrol now accounted for three out of every four litres consumed in Nigeria. He described the development as a major shift for a country that had historically depended heavily on imported petroleum products. However, Umar disclosed that petrol consumption exceeded supply in September, with daily consumption estimated at 44.4 million litres against supply of 38.7 million litres. The shortfall was covered from existing stocks. To guard against future disruptions, he said the Authority was targeting sufficient petroleum product stocks to cover between 30 and 45 days of national demand. Umar also acknowledged that Nigeria lacked reliable data on actual fuel consumption, despite decades of petroleum market operations. “No consumption data yet. We are working on this because up till now no data to show that this fuel station supplied this volume, that supplied that volume,” he said. He explained that the NMDPRA was working with an information technology firm to develop a system capable of tracking distribution and establishing more reliable consumption figures. As part of efforts to improve transparency, the Authority was reviewing internal licences and had signed a memorandum of understanding with the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission. Umar also disclosed that seven petroleum product testing laboratories had been launched in Port Harcourt, with two additional facilities expected before the end of the year, bringing the total to nine. He said the Authority had also launched the second revision of the Gas Transportation Network Code to strengthen the framework governing gas transportation infrastructure. Speaking at the event, President Bola Tinubu said Nigeria’s energy resources could drive prosperity across Africa, reaffirming his administration’s ambition to support the emergence of a regional energy hub. The president whose message was delivered by the Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Petroleum Resources, Mrs. Patience Oyekunle, emphasised the need for regional cooperation and an investment-driven, environmentally responsible energy sector. Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu said energy security was fundamental to economic security, warning that high and unreliable energy costs affected transport fares, manufacturing, food distribution and small businesses. He cited the growth of domestic refining as evidence of changing supply dynamics, noting that the Dangote Refinery produced about 42 million litres of petrol daily in August, while petrol imports fell by 26 per cent to approximately 14.6 million litres per day. Sanwo-Olu said Lagos was also reducing transport fuel demand through investments in rail services and cleaner energy. He disclosed that 152 First and Last Mile buses had been converted to compressed natural gas (CNG), cutting fuel costs by nearly half, while 2,000 CNG-powered trucks had been introduced under haulage reforms. He urged industry stakeholders to prioritise expanded storage and distribution infrastructure, financing for downstream and gas projects, and measures to ensure that the gains from domestic refining translated into stable and affordable prices for consumers. https://dailytrust.com/nigeria-supplies-.title_zh: 尼日利亚9个月内向本地炼油厂供应1.27亿桶原油
https://dailytrust.com/nigeria-supplies-.body_zh: 2026年1月至9月，尼日利亚国内炼油厂接收了逾1.27亿桶尼日利亚原油和凝析油，联邦政府正加大力度发展本地炼油能力，减少对进口石油产品的依赖。尼日利亚上游石油监管委员会（NUPRC）首席执行委员奥里特塞米瓦·艾桑星期一在拉各斯举行的第20届OTL Africa下游能源周活动上披露了这一数据。NUPRC还在就国内原油置换框架征求生产商、炼油商及其他利益相关方的意见。他说：“根据该框架，炼油商可以从最近的合适生产点或出口点接收原油，而不必长距离运输获配原油，这预计可使每桶成本降低3至4美元。”谈及产量，艾桑表示，尼日利亚9月原油和凝析油平均产量为每日171.7万桶，较8月增长2.34%。仅原油一项，平均产量达到每日153万桶，行业连续第五个月完成或超过产量配额。她将这一改善归因于资产完整性提高、外输基础设施安全性增强、与运营商协作更加紧密，以及持续开展监管工作以恢复停产井的产量。她表示，在2026年许可轮次中，推出的40个区块将接受透明评估，评估标准将予以公布，并强制披露受益所有权信息。NUPRC负责人补充说，委员会正在执行“钻探或放弃”原则，遏制投机性持有许可证的行为，并指出近期22名获授权者预计须在五年内至少贡献每日25万桶产量。她重申，委员会致力于履行国内天然气供应义务，并与尼日利亚中下游石油监管局（NMDPRA）合作，使炼油需求与原油供应规划相衔接，确保上游领域的增长切实惠及家庭、产业和电力生产。与此同时，尼日利亚中下游石油监管局（NMDPRA）首席执行委员拉比乌·阿卜杜拉希·乌马尔表示，本地精炼汽油如今占尼日利亚每消费4升汽油中的3升。他称，这一进展对长期严重依赖进口石油产品的尼日利亚而言是一次重大转变。不过，乌马尔透露，9月汽油消费量超过供应量，日消费量估计为4440万升，而供应量为3870万升，缺口由现有库存填补。为防止未来再次出现供应中断，他表示，该局的目标是储备足以覆盖全国30至45天需求的石油产品。乌马尔还承认，尽管尼日利亚的石油市场运营已有数十年，但该国仍缺乏有关实际燃料消费量的可靠数据。他说：“目前仍没有消费数据。我们正在这方面开展工作，因为至今还没有数据证明某座加油站供应了多少燃料、另一座又供应了多少。”他 explained? NMDPRA正与一家信息技术公司合作，开发一套能够追踪供应情况并建立更可靠消费数据的系统。作为提高透明度努力的一部分，该局正在审查内部许可证，并与联邦竞争与消费者保护委员会签署了谅解备忘录。乌马尔还披露，7座石油产品检测实验室已在哈科特港启用，另有两座设施预计将在年底前启用，届时总数将达到9座。他说，该局还启动了《天然气输送网络规范》的第二次修订，以加强天然气输送基础设施的监管框架。总统博拉·蒂努武在活动上表示，尼日利亚的能源资源能够带动非洲各地的繁荣，并重申其政府支持建设区域能源中心的雄心。总统致辞由石油资源部常务秘书帕蒂申·奥耶昆莱女士代为宣读，她强调有必要加强区域合作，建设以投资为动力、对环境负责的能源部门。拉各斯州州长巴巴吉德·桑沃-奥卢表示，能源安全是经济安全的基础，并警告说，能源成本高昂且供应不稳定，会影响交通票价、制造业、食品配送和小企业。他以国内炼油业的增长作为供应格局变化的证据，并指出丹戈特炼油厂8月每日生产约4200万升汽油，而汽油进口量下降26%，降至每日约1460万升。桑沃-奥卢表示，拉各斯还通过投资铁路服务和清洁能源来减少交通燃料需求。他透露，152辆“首末公里”公交车已改装为使用压缩天然气（CNG），使燃料成本降低近一半；运输改革还引入了2000辆CNG动力卡车。他敦促行业利益相关方优先扩大储存和配送基础设施，为下游和天然气项目提供融资，并采取措施确保国内炼油带来的收益转化为消费者稳定且负担得起的价格。加入《每日信任报》WhatsApp社区，快速获取身边的新闻与动态

https://eu.36kr.com/en/p/404291268066291.body: CNCEC's subsidiary signs a low-margin photovoltaic EPC contract in Ghana, testing payment collection capability and project execution capacity. According to the announcement of CNCEC, its subsidiary Sedin Engineering has signed a 300MW photovoltaic EPC contract in Ghana. Four Chinese companies, three West African countries, four completely different market entry strategies. The RMB 2.58 billion deal of CNCEC is the largest among them and the closest to the traditional centralized EPC model. However, it is facing a market where the government has cut the electricity price from 18 cents to 6.5 cents, independent power producers' arrears are still accumulating, and the gross profit margin of photovoltaic EPC has been compressed to a single-digit range. Can an engineering company with a background in coal chemical industry and advanced chemical new materials find its own position in the low-margin photovoltaic sector in West Africa? By the end of 2025, Ghana's cumulative installed photovoltaic capacity reached 276.7MW, of which utility-scale capacity was only 183.1MW, lower than the previously set target of 347.5MW. The updated 2026-2030 plan sets the new ground-mounted photovoltaic target at 852MW, which will be equipped with nearly 2GWh of battery energy storage, and the private sector will undertake 41% of the utility-scale photovoltaic investment. The 300MW single project volume of Sedin exceeds 1.6 times the existing utility-scale photovoltaic stock in Ghana. The figures on the demand side are clear, and even a little urgent. But on the payment side opposite the demand, there is a completely different logic. The Electricity Company of Ghana collects electricity bills in Ghanaian cedi and pays independent power producers in US dollars. Every time the cedi weakens, arrears return to the accounts receivable of independent power producers in the way of "re-accumulation". The Ghanaian Minister of Energy disclosed in October 2026 that the monthly payment ratio to IPPs has increased from about 40% to nearly 100%. The Minister of Finance said that the 2026 budget has allocated 345 million US dollars for energy payments, with the goal of "no new arrears accumulated for the first time". These improvements are real, but they are also political commitments. For an EPC contract with a construction period of two to three years, the sustainability of the commitment is more worthy of attention than the intensity of the commitment. As the EPC contractor, Sedin does not hold the power station assets and does not directly bear the erosion of the cedi depreciation on electricity bill income. However, the release of its progress payment and quality guarantee deposit depends on the rhythm of the owner receiving money from the power purchaser. When the cash flow of the power purchaser is squeezed by the exchange rate, the payment milestones in the EPC contract will be extended first. Low price is not the biggest problem, but the opaque payment path is. In the first half of 2026, CNCEC signed new overseas contracts of 72.935 billion yuan, a year-on-year increase of 76%, and the proportion of overseas revenue rose to 35%; in the first 8 months, the new overseas contracts signed reached 79.188 billion yuan, a year-on-year increase of 57.46%. In emerging tracks such as photovoltaic and energy storage, the company's expression is to "continue to make efforts". The most notable public track record of Sedin in the field of photovoltaic EPC is the 150MW DC project in Laos signed in 2025, with a contract value of 528 million yuan, less than half the scale of the Ghana project. The span from 150MW to 300MW, from Southeast Asia to West Africa, from chemical plants to ground-mounted power stations is obvious. Within the CNCEC system, Hualu Company has long-term accumulation in the engineering of polysilicon materials. The multi-professional interface management, long-cycle equipment procurement rhythm control and overseas on-site construction organization trained by chemical EPC have a considerable proportion of reuse space in ground-mounted photovoltaic power stations. The problem is that what is reused is engineering discipline, not profit thickness. The reason why the gross profit margin of chemical EPC is higher than that of ordinary civil engineering is that the process complexity forms an entry barrier; the process barrier of photovoltaic EPC is much thinner, and the competitors are much denser. If Sedin's 0.86 yuan/W corresponds to a power station body with compressed boundaries, the price is not as aggressive as it seems on the surface; if it corresponds to a more complete scope of work, the profit margin will be further squeezed. The 2.58 billion yuan Ghana project accounts for about 2.6% of CNCEC's total new overseas contracts signed in the first three quarters of 2026, and will not change the overall profit direction alone. But it is a verification sample: Can Sedin turn photovoltaic EPC in Ghana from a one-time "new track breakthrough" into a repeatable business category. If it can, there will be negotiation chips for the second and third projects in West Africa; if not, the 2.58 billion yuan will only be a nice-looking announcement. Looking at the bigger picture, Sedin is not the only Chinese enterprise placing bets in West Africa, but its playstyle is clearly different when compared with several other peers. Sedin's position is heavier than Sungrow's, and lighter than China Energy Engineering's centralized EPC. It does not only earn profits from the manufacturing end like JinkoSolar, nor does it bind the national power company in Senegal to do a 500MW framework like China Energy Engineering. It is taking on a low-margin photovoltaic general contracting project with chemical engineering discipline in a market where electricity prices have been renegotiated and payments are being restored but not yet stable. Sedin's 2.58 billion yuan has bought a ticket to enter the African new energy EPC table. It has already sat at the table. The heaviest chip on the table is not the quotation, but the payment calendar of the Electricity Company of Ghana and who will stand in front of the contractor when the cedi fluctuates next time. https://eu.36kr.com/en/p/404291268066291.title_zh: 中化获得加纳重要光伏订单：这家领先化工企业进入西非利润率最高的细分市场
https://eu.36kr.com/en/p/404291268066291.body_zh: 中国化学旗下子公司在加纳签署低利润率光伏EPC合同，检验回款能力和项目执行能力。据中国化学公告，其子公司塞丁工程已在加纳签署一座300MW光伏EPC合同。4家中资企业、3个西非国家、4种截然不同的市场进入策略。中国化学这笔25.8亿元人民币的交易是其中规模最大的一笔，也最接近传统的集权式EPC模式。然而，该项目面临的市场环境十分严峻：加纳政府已将电价从18美分下调至6.5美分，独立发电商的欠款仍在累积，光伏EPC的毛利率已被压缩至个位数区间。一家拥有煤化工和先进化工新材料背景的工程公司，能否在西非低利润率光伏领域找到自己的位置？截至2025年底，加纳累计光伏装机容量达到276.7MW，其中公用事业规模装机仅为183.1MW，低于此前设定的347.5MW目标。更新后的2026—2030年计划将新建地面光伏目标设定为852MW，并配套近2GWh电池储能，其中私营部门将承担公用事业规模光伏投资的41%。塞丁300MW单体项目的规模超过加纳现有公用事业规模光伏装机的1.6倍。需求端的数据十分清晰，甚至已有些迫切。但与需求端相对，付款端遵循的是一套完全不同的逻辑。加纳电力公司以加纳塞地收取电费，再以美元向独立发电商付款。每当塞地走弱，独立发电商的欠款就会以“重新累积”的方式回到应收账款中。加纳能源部长于2026年10月披露，向独立发电商按月支付的比例已从约40%提高至接近100%。财政部长表示，2026年预算已安排3.45亿美元用于能源付款，目标是“首次不再新增欠款”。这些改善是真实存在的，但同样属于政治承诺。对于建设期为两至三年的EPC合同而言，承诺能否持续比承诺的力度更值得关注。作为EPC承包商，塞丁不持有电站资产，也不直接承受塞地贬值侵蚀电费收入的影响。然而，其进度款和质量保证金的释放取决于业主从购电方收到资金的节奏。当购电方的现金流受到汇率挤压时，EPC合同的付款节点将首先被延后。低价并非最大问题，不透明的付款路径才是。2026年上半年，中国化学新签海外合同729.35亿元，同比增长76%，海外收入占比升至35%；前8个月新签海外合同额达到791.88亿元，同比增长57.46%。在光伏、储能等新兴赛道上，该公司的表述是“继续努力”。塞丁在光伏EPC领域最引人注目的公开业绩，是2025年签署的老挝150MW直流项目，合同金额5.28亿元，不到加纳项目规模的一半。从150MW到300MW，从东南亚到西非，从化工装置到地面电站，各方面的跨越十分明显。在中国化学体系内，华陆公司长期积累的多晶硅材料工程经验具有较高复用价值。化工EPC所形成的多专业接口管理、长周期设备采购节奏控制和海外现场施工组织能力，在地面光伏电站中也有相当大的复用空间。问题在于，复用的是工程纪律，而非利润厚度。化工EPC毛利率高于普通土建工程，是因为工艺复杂度形成了进入壁垒；光伏EPC的工艺壁垒要薄得多，竞争者也密集得多。如果塞丁的0.86元/W对应的是边界被压缩的电站主体，那么这个价格表面上并没有看上去那么激进；如果对应的是更完整的承包范围，利润率还将进一步受到挤压。加纳25.8亿元项目约占中国化学2026年前三季度新签海外合同总额的2.6%，单凭该项目不会改变整体利润走势。但这依然是一个验证样本：塞丁能否把加纳光伏EPC从一次性“新赛道突破”变成可复制的业务品类？如果可以，塞丁在承接西非第二、第三个项目时就掌握了谈判筹码；如果不能，25.8亿元只会是一则好看的公告。放眼全局，押注西非的中国企业并非只有塞丁，但与其他几家同行相比，它的打法明显不同。塞丁的定位比阳光电源更重，又比中国能源建设的集权式EPC更轻。它既不像晶科 solar 那样主要从制造端获利，也不像中国能源建设那样将塞内加尔国家电力公司绑定于500MW框架协议。它是在电价经过重新谈判、付款正在恢复但尚未稳定的市场中，以化工工程的严谨标准承接低利润率光伏总承包项目。塞丁的25.8亿元为其买入了一张进入非洲新能源EPC牌桌的入场券，而它已经坐在了牌桌前。牌桌上最重的筹码不是报价，而是加纳电力公司的付款日程，以及下一次塞地波动时谁会站在承包商前面。中国化学的化工产业基础能够帮助塞丁建设电站，但工程完工后的资金能否沿着从塞地到美元的路径顺利收回，取决于合同结构中是否有相应安排，能够为承包商屏蔽汇率风险。36kr Europe（eu.36kr.com）向全球提供商业和市场新闻、数据、分析及视频，致力于助力企业全球拓展并创造价值、提供商业服务

https://dailytrust.com/what-to-know-as-j.summary: American financial services giant JPMorgan Chase & Co. has moved closer to establishing a merchant bank in Nigeria after receiving approval-in-principle from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), a development that could expand corporate financing options and deepen the country’s access to international capital. https://dailytrust.com/what-to-know-as-j.summary_zh: 美国金融服务巨头JPMorgan Chase & Co.获得尼日利亚中央银行（CBN）原则性批准，在尼日利亚设立商业银行的进程更进一步。这一进展可能扩大企业融资选择，并加深该国获取国际资本的能力。该银行上周获得批准，可继续推进设立JPMorgan Merchant Bank Nigeria Limited的计划，但仍须完成尚未办结的监管及运营要求。
https://dailytrust.com/what-to-know-as-j.body: American financial services giant JPMorgan Chase & Co. has moved closer to establishing a merchant bank in Nigeria after receiving approval-in-principle from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), a development that could expand corporate financing options and deepen the country’s access to international capital. The approval, granted last week allows the bank to proceed with plans to establish JPMorgan Merchant Bank Nigeria Limited, subject to the completion of outstanding regulatory and operational requirements. The development marks a significant step in JPMorgan’s expansion in Africa’s largest economy, where it has maintained a representative office in Lagos for several years. If granted a final licence, the proposed merchant bank would provide a broader platform for the US lender to serve Nigerian corporations, financial institutions and institutional investors. As part of the licensing process, JPMorgan reportedly deposited N50 billion, equivalent to about $38 million, with the CBN to meet the minimum capital requirement for a nationally licensed merchant bank. Daily Trust reports that the deposit fulfilled a key requirement but did not automatically guarantee approval to commence operations. The bank must still satisfy the remaining regulatory conditions, complete the necessary incorporation and operational arrangements, and obtain final authorisation from the CBN before beginning business. JPMorgan had reportedly indicated plans to commence operations before the end of 2026, subject to regulatory clearance. The proposed institution has secured approval for seven board members, including five Nigerians with experience spanning banking, monetary policy, financial technology, law and corporate management. Adedapo Olagunju, who has headed JPMorgan’s West Africa business since 2018, is expected to serve as managing director. He previously held senior positions at Access Bank and Investment Banking & Trust Company, now part of Stanbic IBTC. Chinedum Nzelu Izunwanne, known professionally as Chi Nzelu, is also among the appointees. He is JPMorgan’s global head of macro electronic trading and has experience in foreign exchange, financial technology, automation and risk management. Former acting CBN Governor Sarah Omotunde Alade has been appointed an independent non-executive director. She served as deputy governor of the apex bank from 2007 to 2017 and briefly became acting governor in 2014. She later served as special adviser to the President on finance and the economy. Another independent non-executive director, Olukonyinsola Ajayi, popularly known as Konyin Ajayi, is a partner at Olaniwun Ajayi LP, with expertise in banking, project finance, capital markets, mergers and acquisitions, energy and infrastructure. Seni Adetu, a corporate executive with more than three decades of multinational leadership experience, completes the list of five Nigerian appointees. He previously led Guinness Nigeria and East African Breweries and held senior positions at Coca-Cola and Diageo. Their appointments bring regulatory, financial, legal and corporate expertise to the proposed bank’s leadership. JPMorgan Merchant Bank Nigeria Limited is expected to focus on wholesale banking, corporate finance, structured financing, treasury services, capital markets and advisory services. Its operations could also create opportunities in trade finance, payments, lending and cross-border transactions, depending on the final scope of its licence. For Nigerian businesses, the bank’s entry could provide additional access to international financing networks and specialised financial services, particularly for companies seeking to fund large-scale projects, raise capital or expand into foreign markets. The proposed institution could also strengthen financial relationships between Nigerian businesses and international investors by connecting local companies with JPMorgan’s global corporate and institutional banking network. The proposed expansion comes as Nigeria pursues financial sector reforms aimed at strengthening banking stability, improving investor confidence and attracting foreign capital. JPMorgan’s presence as a locally licensed merchant bank could increase competition in corporate and investment banking while broadening the range of services available to major businesses and institutional clients. On its website, J.P. Morgan describes itself as a global leader in financial services, offering solutions to the world’s most important corporations, governments and institutions in more than 100 countries. For the US banking giant, Nigeria offers access to a large economy with substantial financing needs. For local businesses, its entry could mean more options for capital raising, financial advisory services and international transactions. However, the entry has been generating mixed reactions among economists and financial analysts. Some said the excitement and interest generated by the planned entry of the bank into Nigeria could be as a result of the recent Nigeria-US agreement on mining. It would be recalled that Nigeria and the United States recently signed a framework aimed at unlocking investment in Nigeria’s estimated $700 billion mineral resources and deepening bilateral cooperation in the critical minerals sector. Economist and former banker, Dr. Marcel Okeke in a chat with our correspondent questioned the timing of JPMorgan’s planned entry into Nigeria’s merchant banking sector, suggesting that broader American commercial and strategic interests may be behind the move. Okeke said the decision should be examined against the background of Nigeria’s economic and diplomatic relations with the United States, including a recently signed agreement relating to mineral resources. According to him, JPMorgan’s proposed operation could provide a trusted financial channel for American businesses and investors seeking to pursue opportunities in Nigeria. He argued that the bank’s decision to establish a merchant banking operation, rather than a conventional retail banking business, raises questions about the specific interests it intends to serve. “When you see something that nobody expects to happen, you know that there is a lot behind it,” Okeke said. He added that the broader relationship between Nigeria and the United States could provide important context for understanding the bank’s proposed entry. “You remember recently there was some kind of mineral agreement signed between Nigeria and the US. I don’t have the details of that agreement, but because it involves a lot of money, you have to consider the financial institutions that will be trusted to handle such transactions,” he said. Okeke said JPMorgan’s reputation within the American financial system could make it a preferred institution for facilitating transactions involving American commercial interests in Nigeria. He also questioned why the bank was seeking to establish a merchant bank at a time when security concerns had prompted several countries to issue travel advisories relating to Nigeria. “Why is JPMorgan coming into Nigeria at this particular time, when many countries are issuing travel advisories to their citizens about security concerns in different parts of the country?” he asked. But other analysts see it as a reflection of the ongoing reforms in Nigeria which have brought about renewed investor’s confidence in the Nigeria’s financial system. Ayokunle Olubunmi, a financial analyst said the entry of global financial services giant JPMorgan into Nigeria’s merchant banking sector could improve access to finance, bring international expertise and strengthen support for local businesses. Olubunmi said the bank’s experience across different markets could help introduce Nigerian businesses to financial solutions and transactions that had been successfully deployed elsewhere. He noted that an international financial institution operating across multiple markets could draw on its global expertise to support businesses in Nigeria, while potentially providing access to additional capital. “When a company that is exposed to various markets comes into your country, it brings the experience it has gained in those markets. Some transactions that you may never have thought of have already been carried out elsewhere, and that experience can help,” he said. According to him, JPMorgan’s global reach could also create opportunities for Nigerian businesses to benefit from the bank’s financing capabilities and international networks. https://dailytrust.com/what-to-know-as-j.title_zh: 摩根大通设立商人银行须知
https://dailytrust.com/what-to-know-as-j.body_zh: 美国金融服务巨头JPMorgan Chase & Co.在获得尼日利亚中央银行（CBN）原则性批准后，向在尼日利亚设立商人银行又迈进了一步。此举可能扩大企业融资选择，并深化尼日利亚获取国际资本的渠道。该批准于上周授予，允许该行继续推进设立JPMorgan Merchant Bank Nigeria Limited的计划，但仍须完成尚未办结的监管和运营要求。这是JPMorgan在非洲最大经济体扩张过程中的重要一步，该行已在拉各斯设有代表处多年。如果获得最终牌照，拟议中的商人银行将为这家美国贷款机构提供一个更广泛的平台，服务尼日利亚企业、金融机构和机构投资者。据报道，在牌照审批过程中，JPMorgan向CBN存入500亿奈拉，约合3,800万美元，以满足全国持牌商人银行的最低资本要求。《Daily Trust》报道称，这笔存款满足了一项关键要求，但并不会自动保证获准开始运营。该行仍须满足其余监管条件、完成必要的公司注册和运营安排，并在开始营业前取得CBN的最终授权。据报道，JPMorgan曾表示计划在获得监管放行后于2026年底前开始运营。拟议机构已获准任命7名董事会成员，其中包括5名尼日利亚人，他们拥有银行、货币政策、金融科技、法律和企业管理等方面的经验。自2018年起负责JPMorgan西非业务的Adedapo Olagunju预计将担任董事总经理。他此前曾任Access Bank和Investment Banking & Trust Company高级职位，后者现已成为Stanbic IBTC的一部分。Chinedum Nzelu Izunwanne（职业名为Chi Nzelu）也在获任命人员之列。他是JPMorgan全球宏观电子交易主管，拥有外汇、金融科技、自动化和风险管理方面的经验。尼日利亚中央银行前代理行长Sarah Omotunde Alade已被任命为独立非执行董事。她于2007年至2017年担任该最高银行副行长，并于2014年短暂出任代理行长，后来还担任总统金融与经济问题特别顾问。另一名独立非执行董事Olukonyinsola Ajayi（广为人知名为Konyin Ajayi）是Olaniwun Ajayi LP的合伙人，专长涵盖银行、项目融资、资本市场、并购、能源和基础设施。Seni Adetu拥有逾30年跨国企业管理经验，是一名企业高管，至此5名尼日利亚获任命人员的名单已完成。他曾领导Guinness Nigeria和East African Breweries，并在Coca-Cola和Diageo担任高级职位。这些任命为拟议银行的管理层带来监管、金融、法律和企业管理方面的专长。JPMorgan Merchant Bank Nigeria Limited预计将专注于批发银行、公司融资、结构化融资、资金管理服务、资本市场和咨询服务。根据最终牌照范围，其业务还可能在贸易融资、支付、贷款和跨境交易方面创造机会。对尼日利亚企业而言，该银行进入市场可带来更多接触国际融资网络和专业化金融服务的机会，尤其有利于寻求为大型项目融资、筹集资本或拓展海外市场的企业。拟议机构还可能通过将本地企业接入JPMorgan全球公司及机构银行网络，加强尼日利亚企业与国际投资者之间的金融联系。拟议扩张之际，尼日利亚正推进旨在增强银行体系稳定性、提高投资者信心和吸引外国资本的金融部门改革。JPMorgan以当地持牌商人银行身份进入市场，可能加剧公司和投资银行领域的竞争，同时拓宽大型企业和机构客户可获得的服务范围。J.P. Morgan在其网站上将自身描述为全球金融服务领导者，在100多个国家为全球最重要的企业、政府和机构提供解决方案。对这家美国银行业巨头而言，尼日利亚意味着进入一个融资需求庞大的大型经济体。对当地企业而言，该行进入市场可能意味着更多融资筹措、金融咨询服务和国际交易选择。不过，经济学家和金融分析师对这一进展反应不一。一些人表示，该行计划进入尼日利亚引发的兴奋和关注，可能与尼日利亚和美国近期达成的矿产协议有关。回顾来看，尼日利亚和美国近期签署了一份框架协议，旨在释放尼日利亚估计达7,000亿美元矿产资源的投资潜力，并深化双方在关键矿产领域的合作。经济学家、前银行家Marcel Okeke博士在与本报记者交谈时质疑JPMorgan计划进入尼日利亚商人银行领域的时机，认为此举背后可能涉及更广泛美国商业和战略利益。Okeke表示，应当结合尼日利亚与美国的经济和外交关系审视该决定，其中包括近期签署的矿产资源相关协议。他认为，JPMorgan拟开展的业务可能为寻求在尼日利亚发展机会的美国企业和投资者提供可信的金融渠道。他指出，该行决定开展商人银行业务，而非传统零售银行业务，引发了外界对其打算服务何种特定利益的疑问。Okeke说：“当你看到一件谁都没有预料到会发生的事情时，你就知道其背后有很多因素。”他还补充说，理解该银行拟议进入尼日利亚时，尼日利亚与美国之间的更广泛关系是重要的背景。他说：“你还记得，最近尼日利亚与美国签署了某种矿产协议。我不掌握该协议的细节，但由于涉及巨额资金，你就必须考虑哪些金融机构会获得信任来处理这类交易。”Okeke表示，JPMorgan在美国金融体系中的声誉可能使其成为促成涉及美国在尼日利亚商业利益的交易的首选机构。他还质疑，在安全担忧促使多个国家就尼日利亚发布旅行警示之际，该行为何仍要设立商人银行。他问：“为什么JPMorgan偏偏在这个时候进入尼日利亚？目前许多国家正因对该国不同地区的安全担忧向本国公民发布旅行警示。”但其他分析师认为，这反映了尼日利亚持续推进的改革，以及由此重塑的投资者对尼日利亚金融体系的信心。金融分析师Ayokunle Olubunmi表示，全球金融服务巨头JPMorgan进入尼日利亚商人银行领域，可能改善融资渠道、引入国际专业经验，并加强对本地企业的支持。Olubunmi说，该行在不同市场的经验有助于向尼日利亚企业介绍已在其他市场成功应用的金融解决方案和交易方式。他指出，一家跨多个市场运营的国际金融机构可以运用其全球专业经验支持尼日利亚企业，同时还有望提供更多资本渠道。他说：“当一家与各类市场都有联系的公司来到你的国家时，它会带来自己在这些市场积累的经验。有些你可能从未想过的交易，早已在其他地方完成，而这种经验能够提供帮助。”据他表示，JPMorgan的全球覆盖范围还可能为尼日利亚企业创造机会，使其受益于该行的融资能力和国际网络。加入《Daily Trust》WhatsApp社区，快速获取身边新闻和动态

https://businesspost.ng/general/illegal-.body: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) has arrested 15 suspects, comprising 14 Chinese and one Nigerian, at four illegal lithium processing plants in the Ogere area of Ogun State. The commission disclosed this in a post on its official X account, stating that operatives of its Lagos Zonal Directorate 2 carried out the arrests on Friday, October 23, 2026, following credible intelligence and surveillance. Items recovered during the operation included bags of lithium rocks, 18 mobile devices, four computer laptops, two decoders, a television remote control and a trailer truck. The EFCC said the recovered items had been taken as part of its investigation into the activities of the facilities, adding that the suspects would be charged to court upon the conclusion of investigations. However, the agency did not disclose the specific offences the suspects were alleged to have committed or the ownership of the processing plants. Lithium has become a highly sought-after mineral globally because of its critical role in manufacturing rechargeable batteries used in electric vehicles, smartphones, laptops and renewable energy storage systems. Growing demand for electric vehicles and clean energy technologies has intensified the race to secure lithium supplies, making the mineral increasingly valuable and creating incentives for illegal mining and processing. Nigeria is emerging as a new source of lithium in Africa as the world’s largest producers, like Australia and Chile, are unable to fulfil the growing demand worldwide. However, illegal activities thrive in Nigeria’s extractive sector, denying the government due revenues of up to $9 billion, according to the Nigeria Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (NEITI). The country’s lithium deposits have attracted growing interest from local and foreign operators, while concerns over unregulated extraction, revenue losses, environmental degradation, and the potential circumvention of mining regulations have heightened calls for stricter enforcement. https://businesspost.ng/general/illegal-.body_zh: 经济和金融犯罪委员会（EFCC）在奥贡州奥盖雷地区的4家非法锂加工厂逮捕了15名嫌疑人，其中14名为中国人、1名为尼日利亚人。该委员会在其官方X账号发布的一则消息中披露，拉各斯第2区分局行动人员于2026年10月23日星期五根据可靠情报和监视行动实施了逮捕。行动中缴获的物品包括装在袋中的锂矿石、18部移动设备、4台笔记本电脑、2个解码器、1个电视遥控器和1辆拖挂卡车。EFCC表示，缴获的物品已作为调查这些工厂经营活动的一部分被查扣，并称调查结束后将把嫌疑人移交法院起诉。然而，该机构没有披露嫌疑人被指控实施的具体罪行，也没有披露这些加工厂的归属。锂已成为全球备受追捧的矿产，因为它在制造用于电动汽车、智能手机、笔记本电脑和可再生能源储存系统的可充电电池方面发挥着关键作用。电动汽车和清洁能源技术需求不断增长，加剧了各国争夺锂供应的竞争，使这种矿产的价值日益提高，也刺激了非法采矿和加工活动。随着澳大利亚和智利等全球最大生产国无法满足全球不断增长的需求，尼日利亚正成为非洲新的锂来源。然而，尼日利亚采掘业的非法活动十分猖獗，使政府损失最高达90亿美元的收入，据尼日利亚采掘业透明度倡议（NEITI）称。该国的锂矿藏吸引了越来越多的本地和外国运营商关注，同时，对不受监管的开采、收入流失、环境破坏以及规避采矿法规的担忧，也强化了要求加强执法的呼声。Adedapo Adesanya是一名记者、多才多艺的学者，也是艺术各个领域的行家。不写作时，他不是埋首阅读自己收藏夹中的众多书籍或文章之一，就是拿着一瓶啤酒或葡萄酒聆听好音乐。他支持世界上最伟大的俱乐部——Manchester United F.C.

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/27/l.summary_zh: 拉各斯州政府已向香吉沙地主协会成员分配土地，标志着困扰相关土地所有者、持续寻求司法救济长达40多年的争端取得突破。此次土地分配是在围绕549块土地进行的长期法律诉讼，以及执行2012年作出的最高法院判决之后实现的。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/27/l.body: The Lagos State Government has allocated land to members of the Shangisha Landlords Association, marking a breakthrough in a dispute that has kept affected owners seeking justice for more than four decades. The allocation follows a long legal battle over 549 plots, and enforcement of a Supreme Court judgement delivered in 2012. Landowners and their representatives welcomed the move, as a step towards implementing the court’s decision. Association Chairman, Chief Adebayo Adeyiga, said he was grateful to be alive to witness the development, noting that many original Claimants had died while their children continued the struggle. “We are not going to reject the land”, Adeyiga said, urging the State to provide access roads and other infrastructure to make the site habitable. He also called for respect for court judgements, saying disputes should not persist after a Supreme Court ruling. The Baale of Shangisha, Yusuf Mutiu Ogundare, and the Onirolu of Irolu, Oba Sikiru Adeyiga, one of the judgement creditors, also thanked the State Government, the IG of Police and officials involved. Counsel to the Judgement creditors, Deji Fasusi, described the allocation as a triumph of the rule of law. He urged the Government to also provide site services, access roads and complete the remaining allocations promptly. Fasusi appealed to residents to remain patient and cooperate with the authorities, as the process continues. Earlier, Lagos State Solicitor-General and Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Justice, Hameed Oyenuga, representing Attorney-General Lawal Pedro, SAN, presented a map of the allocated area and explained the distribution process. While celebrating this settlement, the landowners say the breakthrough must now be matched by infrastructure and full implementation. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/27/l.body_zh: 拉各斯州政府已向尚吉沙地主协会成员分配土地，标志着在一场导致相关土地所有者寻求正义逾40年的争端中取得突破。此次分配是在围绕549块土地展开的长期法律斗争，以及执行2012年作出的最高法院判决之后进行的。土地所有者及其代表对这一举措表示欢迎，认为这是落实法院裁决的一步。协会主席阿德巴约·阿德伊加酋长表示，他很感激能在世见证这一进展，并指出许多原始索赔人已经去世，而他们的子女仍在继续抗争。阿德伊加说：“我们不会拒绝这些土地”，并敦促州政府修建通道路和提供其他基础设施，使该地点适宜居住。他还呼吁尊重法院判决，表示最高法院作出裁决后，纠纷不应继续悬而未决。尚吉沙的巴阿里·尤素夫·穆蒂乌·奥贡达雷，以及伊罗卢的奥尼罗卢、判决债权人之——奥巴·西基鲁·阿德伊加，也向州政府、警察总长和相关官员致谢。判决债权人的律师德吉·法苏西称，这次分配是法治的胜利。他敦促政府同时提供场地服务、通道路，并迅速完成剩余分配。法苏西呼吁居民保持耐心，并与当局合作，因为相关程序仍在继续。此前，代表总检察长拉瓦勒·佩德罗律师的拉各斯州总检察长兼司法部常任秘书哈米德·奥耶努加提交了已分配区域的地图，并解释了分配流程。在庆祝这一解决方案的同时，土地所有者表示，此次突破如今必须以完善的基础设施和全面落实为支撑。THISDAY创刊于1995年1月22日，由THISDAY NEWSPAPERS LTD.出版，地址为尼日利亚拉各斯阿帕帕溪路35号，在尼日利亚36个州、联邦首都辖区及世界各地设有办公室。该报是尼日利亚最具权威性的新闻媒体，通过所有平台为政治、商业、专业和外交精英以及更广泛的中产阶级提供服务，同时充当有抱负者和千禧一代探索新思想、文化与技术的交汇点。这份报纸是一项公共信托，致力于追求真相与理性，报道从突发新闻到政治、商业、金融市场、艺术、体育和社区等各类议题，呈现人与社会的交汇面貌。您可以发送邮件至：hello@thisdaylive.com，或访问我们的联系我们页面

https://www.myjoyonline.com/sammy-gyamfi.summary: The Centre for Mining Research and Policy has rejected the Minority’s call for the resignation of Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) Chief Executive Officer Sammy Gyamfi over his comments on the formalisation of small-scale mining. The Centre said the call was not justified, arguing that Mr Gyamfi’s position focused on bringing eligible small-scale miners into the formal regulatory system rather than allowing illegal mining to continue.
https://www.myjoyonline.com/sammy-gyamfi.summary_zh: 矿业研究与政策中心驳回了少数族群要求加纳黄金局（GoldBod）首席执行官 Sammy Gyamfi 辞职的呼吁，原因是其就小规模采矿正规化发表的言论。该中心表示，这一要求没有依据，并认为 Gyamfi 先生的立场旨在推动符合资格的小规模采矿者纳入正式监管体系，而非纵容非法采矿继续存在。
https://www.myjoyonline.com/sammy-gyamfi.body: The Centre for Mining Research and Policy has rejected the Minority’s call for the resignation of Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) Chief Executive Officer Sammy Gyamfi over his comments on the formalisation of small-scale mining. The Centre said the call was not justified, arguing that Mr Gyamfi’s position focused on bringing eligible small-scale miners into the formal regulatory system rather than allowing illegal mining to continue. Senior Research Fellow at the Centre, Dr Ofori Kodua, said Mr Gyamfi had made it clear that eligible operators must obtain the necessary documentation, permits, certification and training to operate legally. He added that the GoldBod CEO had condemned mining activities that destroy water bodies, encroach on forest reserves or endanger communities. The Ghana National Association of Small Scale Miners, which co-organised the engagement at which the disputed remarks were made, has also defended their context. According to the association, the excerpt circulated from the event gave a misleading impression of a discussion about registering and regularising eligible operators. The Centre said the Minority’s demand for Mr Gyamfi’s resignation did not adequately consider that explanation. It also cited GoldBod’s reported performance in the small-scale gold trading sector as a reason to continue supporting the board’s reforms. According to the figures provided by GoldBod, the institution aggregated and exported 85.4 tonnes of small-scale gold valued at US$11.6 billion between January and October 20, 2026. The Centre said the figures demonstrated the economic importance of the sector and the need to strengthen official channels for gold trading. It further pointed to GoldBod’s reported support for anti-illegal-mining operations and funding for the reclamation of 50 hectares in the Tano Nimiri Forest Reserve. The board is also procuring a traceability system intended to establish the lawful origin of gold moving through the supply chain. The Centre acknowledged that the initiatives would require effective implementation and scrutiny but argued that they provided grounds for continued engagement with GoldBod’s reform agenda. It maintained that small-scale mining formalisation must be tied to compliance with licensing requirements, safer practices and regulatory supervision, while destructive mining should be subject to enforcement action. The Centre therefore called on the Minority to focus on scrutinising the implementation and results of the reforms rather than demanding Mr Gyamfi’s removal. It also cited GoldBod’s engagement with the World Gold Council on formalisation, traceability and responsible processing as evidence of efforts to align Ghana’s domestic priorities with international expertise. The Centre said Mr Gyamfi should be allowed to continue leading the reforms, while his performance and the outcomes of the initiatives remain subject to public and parliamentary scrutiny
https://www.myjoyonline.com/sammy-gyamfi.title_zh: 采矿研究与政策中心：Sammy Gyamfi关于采矿正规化的言论不足以构成辞职理由
https://www.myjoyonline.com/sammy-gyamfi.body_zh: 矿业研究与政策中心驳回了少数派要求加纳黄金局（GoldBod）首席执行官 Sammy Gyamfi 辞职的呼吁，原因是他就小规模采矿正规化发表的言论。该中心表示，这项要求没有依据，并称 Gyamfi 先生的立场重点是推动符合条件的小规模采矿者纳入正式监管体系，而非纵容非法采矿继续进行。该中心高级研究员 Ofori Kodua 博士表示，Gyamfi 先生已明确指出，符合条件的经营者必须取得合法运营所需的文件、许可证、认证并接受培训。他还表示，加纳黄金局首席执行官谴责了破坏水体、侵占森林保护区或危及社区的采矿活动。共同组织争议言论发生交流活动的加纳全国小规模矿工协会，也为其发表言论的背景进行了辩护。据该协会称，活动结束后流传的节选内容使人误以为，讨论的是为符合条件的经营者办理登记和正规化手续。该中心表示，少数派要求 Gyamfi 先生辞职时，未充分考虑这一解释。该中心还援引加纳黄金局公布的小规模黄金交易行业业绩，作为继续支持该局改革的理由。根据加纳黄金局提供的数据，2026年1月至10月20日，该机构共汇集并出口了85.4吨小规模黄金，价值116亿美元。该中心表示，这些数据证明该行业具有重要的经济意义，也说明有必要加强黄金交易的官方渠道。该中心还指出，加纳黄金局据报支持打击非法采矿的行动，并为塔诺尼米里森林保护区50公顷土地的修复提供资金。该局还在采购一套可追溯系统，用于确定进入供应链的黄金的合法来源。该中心承认，这些举措需要有效实施和监督，但认为它们为继续参与加纳黄金局的改革议程提供了依据。该中心坚持认为，小规模采矿正规化必须与遵守许可要求、采用更安全作业方式和接受监管监督相结合，同时应对破坏性采矿采取执法行动。因此，该中心呼吁少数派把重点放在审查改革措施的实施情况和成效上，而不是要求 Gyamfi 先生下台。该中心还援引加纳黄金局与世界黄金协会就正规化、可追溯性和负责任加工开展合作的事例，证明其正努力推动加纳国内优先事项与国际专业经验相衔接。该中心表示，应允许 Gyamfi 先生继续领导改革，同时其履职表现和各项举措的成果仍应接受公众和议会的监督

https://www.myjoyonline.com/malawi-deleg.body: Malawi is looking to Ghana’s experience in gold production and mining-sector reforms for lessons to strengthen its own mineral governance, with a focus on responsible sourcing, artisanal mining and the financing of mineral-related businesses. The delegation, led by Malawi’s Minister of Mining, Thoko Tembo, met Ghana’s Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah, as part of a learning mission supported by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP). The engagement focused on Ghana’s mining governance framework and ongoing efforts to improve gold purchasing, traceability, production accounting and the management of mineral revenues. Mr Buah said Ghana’s long history of mining had provided experience from which other countries could learn, while emphasising that the country was also working to improve its policies and regulatory systems. He said ongoing reforms were intended to strengthen accountability in the gold sector, protect the environment and ensure mining communities had a greater voice and benefited from resources extracted from their lands. The Lands Minister outlined proposed changes to the mining licensing regime, including clearer timelines and performance requirements for companies holding mining rights. He also highlighted plans to involve district-level mining committees in assessing proposed concessions before licences are issued. The proposed measures are intended to strengthen oversight and improve the assessment of mining proposals before they receive regulatory approval. Chief Executive Officer of the Minerals Commission, Isaac Tandoh, also presented Ghana’s mining governance framework to the delegation. He responded to questions on domestic gold purchasing, the formalisation of mineral markets and efforts to strengthen responsible sourcing systems. Malawi’s Minister of Mining, Thoko Tembo, welcomed the opportunity to learn from Ghana’s experience, including challenges encountered in developing and regulating its mining industry. He said the delegation wanted practical lessons that could help Malawi avoid similar difficulties as it develops its own sector. The discussions included artisanal and small-scale mining and access to financing for businesses operating in the minerals industry. The delegation also included representatives of Malawi’s banking sector and artisanal and small-scale mining industry, reflecting an interest in both regulatory approaches and the financial systems needed to support mineral-sector development. The engagement provided an opportunity for the two countries to exchange perspectives on mining regulation, domestic mineral markets and responsible sourcing. For Ghana, the discussions come as authorities pursue reforms aimed at improving accountability in gold purchasing and strengthening oversight of mining activities. For Malawi, the visit offers an opportunity to examine Ghana’s policy approaches and consider which lessons could inform the development of its own mining industry
https://www.myjoyonline.com/malawi-deleg.title_zh: 马拉维代表团考察加纳矿业改革及负责任的黄金治理
https://www.myjoyonline.com/malawi-deleg.body_zh: 马拉维正借鉴加纳在黄金生产和矿业部门改革方面的经验，以加强自身矿产治理，重点关注负责任采购、手工采矿以及矿产相关企业的融资。由马拉维矿业部长托科·腾博率领的代表团会见了加纳土地与自然资源部长埃马纽埃尔·阿马-科菲·布阿。此次学习访问得到联合国开发计划署（UNDP）支持。交流重点围绕加纳的矿业治理框架，以及加纳正在推进的黄金收购、可追溯性、生产核算和矿产收入管理改进工作。布阿表示，加纳悠久的采矿历史积累了可供其他国家借鉴的经验，同时强调加纳也在努力完善政策和监管体系。他说，持续推进的改革旨在加强黄金行业问责、保护环境，并确保采矿社区拥有更大发言权，且能从其土地上开采的资源中获得更多利益。土地部长介绍了拟对矿业许可制度作出的调整，包括为持有采矿权的公司设定更明确的时间要求和绩效要求。他还强调，计划在颁发许可证之前，让地区级矿业委员会参与评估拟议的采矿特许权。这些拟议措施旨在加强监督，并改善对矿业项目在获得监管批准前的评估。矿产委员会首席执行官艾萨克·坦多赫也向代表团介绍了加纳的矿业治理框架，并就国内黄金收购、矿产市场正规化以及加强负责任采购体系的努力回答了问题。马拉维矿业部长托科·腾博对有机会借鉴加纳经验表示欢迎，其中包括开发和监管本国矿业过程中所遇到的挑战。他说，代表团希望获得切实可行的经验，以帮助马拉维在发展本国矿业时避免类似困难。讨论内容涵盖手工采矿和小规模采矿，以及矿产行业企业获得融资的问题。代表团成员还包括马拉维银行业以及手工采矿和小规模采矿行业的代表，反映出双方既关注监管方法，也关注支持矿产行业发展的金融体系。此次交流为两国提供了就矿业监管、国内矿产市场和负责任采购交换观点的机会。对加纳而言，相关讨论正值当局推进旨在提高黄金收购问责和加强对采矿活动监督的改革之际。对马拉维而言，此次访问提供了一个考察加纳政策做法，并思考哪些经验可以为本国矿业发展提供借鉴的机会

https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.title: Alleged Certificate Forgery: UNN, NYSC disowned Nnaji’s certificates, witness tells court
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.summary: A prosecution witness, on Monday, told the Federal High Court in Abuja that the University of Nigeria, Nsukka (UNN), and the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) disowned certificates linked to former Minister of Innovation, Science and Technology, Geoffrey Nnaji. The witness further told the court that UNN also responded that Nnaji failed to obtain the required grades for the award of his certificate.
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.summary_zh: 周一，一名控方证人在阿布贾联邦高等法院表示，尼日利亚大学恩苏卡分校（UNN）和国家青年服务团（NYSC）均否认签发与前创新、科技部长杰弗里·纳贾有关联的证书。该证人进一步告诉法院，UNN 还回应称，纳贾未取得授予其证书所需的成绩。
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.body: A prosecution witness, on Monday, told the Federal High Court in Abuja that the University of Nigeria, Nsukka (UNN), and the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) disowned certificates linked to former Minister of Innovation, Science and Technology, Geoffrey Nnaji. The witness, who identified himself as Yakubu Ibrahim, a superintendent of police officer with the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC), made the revelation. He was led in evidence by prosecution lawyer J.A Mumini, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN). ICPC is prosecuting Mr Nnaji on certificate forgery and money laundering charges. An investigation by PREMIUM TIMES exposed the certificate forgery scandal leading to Mr Nnaji’s ouster from office last year. The former minister is the Peoples Democratic Party’s governorship candidate for the upcoming 2027 governorship candidate in Enugu State. Mr Ibrahim said his team was assigned to investigate the matter after the commission received two separate petitions alleging certificate forgery against Mr Nnaji. He said the Chairman of the Special Task Force directed an investigation, prompting the commission to request relevant documents from the National Assembly, the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), University of Nigeria, Nsukka and the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC). According to him, the Clerk of the Senate, National Assembly, forwarded Mr Nnaji’s NYSC certificate and BSc certificate in Microbiology and Biochemistry to the commission. He said NYSC responded that the certificate purportedly issued by the corps was not issued by it. The witness further told the court that UNN also responded that Nnaji failed to obtain the required grades for the award of his certificate. He said the university explained in its letter the policy governing the grades required for the award of a certificate saying if one failed four times, the person was not qualified. Mr Ibrahim said Mr Nnaji failed at two stages and did not write the examination at the third stage for medical reasons. “The witness said that, according to the letter, the defendant went ahead to write the supplementary examination for which he did not register,” he said. Mr Ibrahim further testified that UNN confirmed that the BSc certificate in Microbiology and Biochemistry attributed to the defendant was not issued by the university. He said the commission also obtained documents from the SGF’s office, including a payslip, which prompted it to request Mr Nnaji’s bank statement. According to him, the bank statement showed that Mr Nnaji received N29.5 million in salary as minister before he resigned . The witness identified letters sent to the Clerk of the Senate, the SGF, UNN, NYSC, the bank and Mr Nnaji, which were tendered in evidence. He also told the court that Mr Nnaji failed to honour the commission’s invitation to answer questions on the petitions, prompting the ICPC to contact the State Security Service (SSS). Mr Nnaji’s lawyer, Wole Olanipekun, a SAN, said he would reserve his objection to the admissibility of the documents until the appropriate stage of the proceedings, if necessary. In a ruling, Judge Joyce Abdulmalik admitted the documents in evidence but held that objections to their admissibility would be reserved until the final address. During cross-examination by Mr Olanipekun, Mr Ibrahim told the court that he did not visit UNN during his investigation. He also said he did not know how many campuses the university had or the faculty from which Mr Nnaji graduated. Asked whether he interviewed any past or present university staff member, the witness said he interviewed a registrar named Ngozi but could not recall her surname. Mr Ibrahim also told the court that he saw a letter from UNN directing the withdrawal of Mr Nnaji’s admission. Mr Olanipekun, however, drew his attention to another letter showing that the withdrawal letter dated 7 November 1984, was rescinded by a subsequent letter dated 18 March 1985. With no further questions from the defence for the witness, the prosecution requested an adjournment to enable it call another witness. Ms Abdulmalik adjourned the matter until 5 November for continuation of trial. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that Nnaji was arraigned before the Federal High Court on six counts of certificate forgery, money laundering and abuse of office. The ICPC, which filed the charges, alleged that Mr Nnaji presented forged UNN degree and NYSC certificates to support his ministerial appointment in 2023. The commission also accused him of receiving about N29.58 million in salaries and allowances as minister, allegedly linked to proceeds of unlawful acts. The court granted him bail in yhe sum of N20 million with one surety and he was ordered to deposit his passport with the court. He is not to travel outside the country without permission from the court throughout the period of his trial
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.title_zh: 涉嫌伪造证书：证人在法庭上称UNN和NYSC否认Nnaji的证书
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.body_zh: 周一，一名控方证人在阿布贾联邦高等法院表示，尼日利亚大学恩苏卡分校（UNN）和国家青年服务团（NYSC）均否认签发与前创新、科技部长Geoffrey Nnaji有关联的证书。自称尼日利亚独立腐败预防及其他相关罪行委员会（ICPC）警监Yakubu Ibrahim的证人披露了此事。控方律师、尼日利亚资深大律师（J.A Mumini）引导他作证。ICPC正以伪造证书和洗钱罪名起诉Nnaji先生。PREMIUM TIMES的调查揭露了这起伪造证书丑闻，导致Nnaji先生去年被免职。这位前部长是人民民主党在埃努古州即将举行的2027年州长选举中的候选人。Ibrahim先生表示，委员会收到两份分别指控Nnaji先生伪造证书的申诉后，指派其团队调查此事。他说，特别任务组主席指示展开调查，促使委员会向国家议会、联邦政府秘书办公室（SGF）、尼日利亚大学恩苏卡分校和国家青年服务团（NYSC）索取相关文件。据他介绍，国家议会参议院书记官转交给委员会Nnaji先生的国家青年服务团证书以及微生物学和生物化学理学士学位证书。他说，NYSC回复称，声称由该团签发的证书并非其签发。证人进一步告诉法庭，UNN也回复称，Nnaji未达到获颁证书所需的成绩。他说，学校在信函中解释了取得证书所适用的成绩政策：若有4次不及格，该人士便不具备资格。Ibrahim先生说，Nnaji先生在两个阶段未能通过考试，并因医疗原因没有参加第三个阶段的考试。他说：“证人表示，根据信函，被告仍参加了补考，尽管他并未为补考报名。”Ibrahim先生进一步作证称，UNN确认 attributed to the defendant 的微生物学和生物化学理学士学位证书并非由该大学签发。他说，委员会还从SGF办公室取得了包括工资单在内的文件，并据此要求提供Nnaji先生的银行账单。据他介绍，银行账单显示，Nnaji先生担任部长期间收取了29.5 million naira薪金，之后辞职。证人确认了发给参议院书记官、SGF、UNN、NYSC、银行及Nnaji先生的信函，并将其作为证据提交。他还告诉法庭，Nnaji先生未按委员会要求接受询问、就申诉回答问题，促使ICPC联系了国家安全局（SSS）。Nnaji先生的律师、尼日利亚资深大律师Wole Olanipekun表示，如有必要，他将在诉讼程序的适当阶段再对这些文件能否采纳提出异议。法官Joyce Abdulmalik裁定准许将这些文件作为证据，但表示关于其可采性的异议将留待最终陈词阶段处理。在Olanipekun先生交叉询问期间，Ibrahim先生告诉法庭，他在调查期间没有前往UNN。他还说，自己不知道该校有多少个校区，也不知道Nnaji先生毕业于哪个学院。问他是否询问过该大学任何过去或现任工作人员，证人说，他询问过一名名为Ngozi的注册主任，但无法想起她的姓氏。Ibrahim先生还告诉法庭，他看到了一封来自UNN、要求撤销Nnaji先生入学资格的信函。然而，Olanipekun先生提请他注意另一封信，该信显示，日期为1984年11月7日的撤销入学信函已被日期为1985年3月18日的后续信函撤销。辩方没有再向该证人提问后，控方请求休庭，以便传唤另一名证人。Abdulmalik女士将案件延期至11月5日继续审理。尼日利亚通讯社（NAN）报道称，Nnaji因6项伪造证书、洗钱和滥用职权罪名被带到联邦高等法院受审。提出指控的ICPC称，Nnaji先生提交了伪造的UNN学位证书和NYSC证书，以支持其于2023年获任部长。委员会还指控他担任部长期间收取约29.58 million naira的薪金和津贴，称这些款项涉嫌与非法所得有关。法院准许其以20 million naira保释，条件是提供一名担保人，并命令他将护照交由法院保管。在整个审判期间，未经法院许可，他不得离开该国。

https://dailytrust.com/2027-elections-10.summary: The electorate is bigger than ever and the field more fragmented, but the outcome may turn less on what voters think than on which of them actually vote. https://dailytrust.com/2027-elections-10.summary_zh: 选民人数比以往任何时候都多，阵营也更加分散，但最终结果与其说取决于选民怎么想，不如说取决于他们实际上谁会投票。假设选民偏好保持不变——廷努布的支持者继续支持廷努布，阿提库的继续支持阿提库，奥比的继续支持奥比，夸恩克瓦索的继续支持夸恩克瓦索——仅改变投票率。将2023年全国投票率26.71%统一套用于新选民名册，计算结果显示，廷努布先生获得960万票，奥比—夸恩克瓦索组合获得897万票，阿提库先生获得723万票。
https://dailytrust.com/2027-elections-10.body: If Nigerians vote as they did in 2023 but more of them turn up, the race for Aso Rock looks very different. Turnout in the South-East, Kano’s Kwankwaso machine, four state reversals and a regional upstart may matter more than any change of heart. Nigerians will choose a president in fewer than 100 days, most of them preoccupied with insecurity and the soaring cost of living. Yet the election holds a paradox. The electorate is bigger than ever and the field more fragmented, but the outcome may turn less on what voters think than on which of them actually vote. Start with the numbers. The register has swollen to 103.4m, from 93.5m in 2023. State-by-state results from the last election, compiled by Vanguard and Stears , supply the map. Hold preferences constant – Tinubu voters stay with Tinubu, Atiku’s with Atiku, Obi’s with Obi and Kwankwaso’s with Kwankwaso – and change only turnout. The map starts to misbehave. A caveat: this is a scenario, not a forecast or a poll. It combines the 2026-27 register with 2023 state-level vote shares, then layers on assumptions – constructed turnout rates, an Obi–Kwankwaso merger, swapped vote shares in Plateau, Osun, Taraba and Bayelsa, and a hypothetical Makinde–Bala ticket on the APM platform in Bauchi and Oyo. Later sections test direct switches between Mr Tinubu and Mr Atiku. Nor does the model adjust for rigging. It does not need to: the 2023 results were challenged all the way to the Supreme Court on grounds of irregularities and upheld. Whatever irregularities occurred are therefore already built into the legally settled baseline on which these projections rest. In 2023 Mr Peter Obi ran up huge margins in parts of the South, but many of his strongholds turned out only modestly. Mr Bola Tinubu and Mr Abubakar Atiku, by contrast, drew heavily on high-turnout states. Apply the 2023 national turnout of 26.71% uniformly to the new register and the arithmetic gives Mr Tinubu 9.60m votes, an Obi–Kwankwaso ticket 8.97m and Mr Atiku 7.23m. The merger alone transforms the race. The more interesting question is what happens if low-turnout areas start behaving like high-turnout ones. Take Anambra and Kano. Suppose Anambra’s voters, instead of repeating their lacklustre 2023 showing, turned out at roughly Kano’s rate. Extend that across Mr Obi’s 2023 winning states: a turnout floor of 31.7%, with higher historical rates kept wherever they already exceeded it. The result flips. Obi–Kwankwaso edges ahead with 10.14m votes to Mr Tinubu’s 10.06m, with Mr Atiku on 7.51m – a margin of barely 85,000. That should unsettle every party headquarters. Mr Obi may not need to win in 2027 over millions of 2023 Tinubu voters; he may first need to get more of his own sympathisers to the polls. Two can play that game. Give Mr Atiku’s states the same treatment, however, and the advantage evaporates. Higher turnout in Adamawa, Bauchi, Gombe, Kaduna, Katsina, Kebbi, Osun, Sokoto, Taraba, Yobe and the rest of his territory does not help him alone, because his rivals also polled heavily there. Mr Tinubu returns to the lead with about 11.05m votes, against 10.50m for Obi–Kwankwaso and 8.83m for Mr Atiku. Do the same for Mr Tinubu’s states and turnout climbs towards 34.7m, roughly 33.6% of the register: Mr Tinubu 12.16m, Obi–Kwankwaso 10.79m, Mr Atiku 9.51m. The incumbent’s structural advantage reasserts itself. The lesson: mobilisation cannot be judged in isolation. If everyone gets out the vote equally well, the advantage returns to the coalition with the best mix of geographical spread, big-state strength and respectable second places. Elections are not reruns, so introduce some movement. Suppose Plateau, which Mr Obi won in 2023, swings to Mr Tinubu; rather than invent a swing, simply swap the two men’s 2023 vote shares. Do the same for three of Mr Atiku’s states – Osun, Taraba and Bayelsa – drifting towards Mr Tinubu. Mr Tinubu rises to about 12.48m; Obi–Kwankwaso slips to 10.62m and Mr Atiku to 9.35m. His lead stretches to some 1.86m. Four states have changed the complexion of the race. Enter the spoiler. Now add a Makinde–Bala ticket on the APM platform that concentrates on just two states: Bauchi, Mr Atiku’s in 2023, and Oyo, Mr Tinubu’s. In each, the previous winner is demoted to runner-up and the newcomer takes the winning share. That gives the APM about 584,000 votes in Bauchi and 601,000 in Oyo – some 1.18m from two states alone. A four-way race. Under the full scenario, turnout reaches about 35m. Mr Tinubu wins 11.69m votes (33.67%), Obi–Kwankwaso 10.62m (30.58%), Mr Atiku 8.96m (25.79%) and Makinde–Bala 1.18m (3.41%); other candidates share the remaining 2.2m (6.55%). Mr Tinubu still leads, but by only a little more than one million. Note what did not happen. Nobody conjured an electoral revolution. The exercise merely enlarged the electorate, nudged turnout, merged two camps, moved four states and added a regional challenger. Yet the lead changed hands, and the winning margin ranged from 85,000 to 1.86m. Much hinges on turnout, nowhere more than in the South-East, whose five states hold about 11.98m registered voters. But registration confers no clout by itself: a voter who stays at home counts for exactly as much as one who never registered. Turnout may be the great hidden variable of 2027. Lagos has nearly 7.5m registered voters. At 31.7% turnout that means almost 2.4m ballots. On 2023 shares, Obi–Kwankwaso takes about 1.05m to Mr Tinubu’s 1.02m – a statistical dead heat. A shift of a few tens of thousands could tip the national result. Lagos is worth not merely winning, but winning well. The art of losing well. Perhaps the least intuitive lesson is that the presidential race is not 37 winner-takes-all contests. A candidate who loses a state 45 to 40 still banks his 40. Winning more states is a different strategy from maximising the national vote while keeping enough geographical spread. Kingmakers, not kings. With 1.18m votes, Makinde–Bala is nowhere near first place. Yet its effect could be outsized, because it does not draw votes evenly: in Bauchi it hurts mainly Mr Atiku, in Oyo mainly Mr Tinubu. A small fourth candidate concentrated in the right states can wield influence out of all proportion to its national share. Whoever comes fourth could help decide who comes first. The model boils the election down to four linked contests. The first is over turnout: can low-participation strongholds vote in greater numbers without their rivals doing the same? The second is over coalitions: Obi–Kwankwaso looks formidable because it pairs strength in the South-East, the Middle Belt and Lagos with Mr Kwankwaso’s following in Kano. The third concerns defecting states: Plateau, Osun, Taraba and Bayelsa show how a handful of plausible shifts can move hundreds of thousands of net votes. The fourth is the spoiler contest, in which a Makinde–Bala-style ticket matters without ever being nationally competitive. A frightening number. Mr Tinubu’s final lead of a little more than one million is roughly 1% of a register of more than 103m. With only about a third of registered voters turning out, modest changes among today’s non-voters could easily swamp it. Keep the swaps and turnout alone cannot do it. The break-even rate against Mr Tinubu rises to about 121% – a mathematical impossibility. Even at 100% turnout in all 12 states, Mr Tinubu polls 18.02m to Mr Atiku’s 17.37m, a lead of some 656,000.Why is the bar so high? First, extra turnout is shared: with 2023 shares fixed, Mr Tinubu and Obi–Kwankwaso also gain, notably in Katsina, Kebbi, Sokoto, Osun and Bauchi, where Mr Tinubu was a competitive runner-up. Second, with the APM taking the winning share in Bauchi, a higher turnout there helps Makinde–Bala more than it does Mr Atiku. Third, in Bayelsa, Osun and Taraba, Mr Tinubu now holds the larger share, so every extra voter there widens his lead. At 1m switches, Mr Tinubu and Obi–Kwankwaso are separated by about 75,000 votes, with Mr Atiku still third. Only at around 2m does he move clear, leading Obi–Kwankwaso by about 339,000 and Mr Tinubu by about 1.26m. The crucial word is net. Every southern Atiku voter who drifts to Mr Tinubu adds one to the northern requirement: lose 500,000 in the South, and he needs about 2.16m converts (38.6% of Mr Tinubu’s 2023 northern vote); lose 1m, and he needs 2.66m (47.5%). Even with no southern losses, a comfortable 500,000-vote victory would take about 2.16m switches. It is tempting to split Nigeria into a northern Atiku constituency and a southern Tinubu one. The arithmetic is messier. In 2023 Mr Tinubu led Mr Atiku across the 19 northern states and the FCT by only about 365,000 votes, against roughly 1.46m in the South. Split the North further, and the picture sharpens. Across the North-West and North-East – the Core North – Mr Atiku actually won, by about 234,000. That conceals two contests: Mr Tinubu took the North-West by some 323,000, Mr Atiku the North-East by about 556,000. In other words, “Atiku takes the North, Tinubu takes the South” largely happened in 2023. Mr Atiku’s problem was scale: Mr Tinubu’s southern margin was more than six times his Core North advantage. Between the two blocs sits the North-Central, which should not be treated as an appendage of the Core North. In 2023 it split three ways: Mr Tinubu won about 1.76m votes, Mr Obi and Mr Kwankwaso together about 1.48m and Mr Atiku about 1.16m. Mr Tinubu carried Benue, Kogi, Kwara and Niger; Mr Obi took Nasarawa, Plateau and the FCT. With APC-leaning territory, old PDP constituencies, strong Obi support and ethnically and religiously mixed electorates, it is a genuine swing belt. A 10% transfer of Mr Tinubu’s North-Central vote to Mr Atiku would move about 176,000 votes and swing their head-to-head margin by about 352,000 – meaningful, but not decisive alone. Its leverage lies in amplifying a Core North recovery or protecting a southern lead. Now strip out the turnout boosts, swaps and spoiler and return to the plain baseline: 26.71% turnout applied to each state’s share of the 103.4m register, with 2023 vote shares held state by state. About 27.6m votes are cast across three theatres. The 2023 pattern survives, but its scale changes. Mr Atiku’s Core North lead shrinks to about 132,000, while Mr Tinubu’s southern lead swells to almost 1.9m – more than fourteen times as large. And the North-Central is far from neutral: it hands Mr Tinubu a further 610,000. Before a single southern vote is counted, he is about 479,000 ahead across the North and the FCT. Now test a reciprocal realignment: a share of Mr Tinubu’s Core North voters switches to Mr Atiku, while the same share of Mr Atiku’s southern voters switches to Mr Tinubu, with the North-Central unchanged. Equal percentages are not equal numbers. Mr Tinubu’s Core North pool (3.88m) is nearly twice Mr Atiku’s southern one (2.10m), so at 10% about 388,000 northern voters move to Mr Atiku and only about 210,000 southern voters to Mr Tinubu. The paradox is that both men grow stronger, in different halves of the country. At 15%, Mr Atiku leads the Core North by almost 1.3m, yet Mr Tinubu leads the South by about 2.52m and the country by about 1.84m. Drawing from the larger pool, Mr Atiku closes the gap, but slowly: across the two blocs, break-even comes at about 49.4% – nearly half of Mr Tinubu’s Core North support defecting while the same share of Mr Atiku’s southern vote goes the other way. That is not a swing but a realignment, and it would still leave Mr Tinubu’s 610,000 North-Central cushion intact. A northern recovery is therefore necessary for Mr Atiku but not sufficient: he must also stop the PDP’s residual southern vote in Rivers, Oyo, Ogun, Akwa Ibom and beyond from shrinking. That makes the North-West arguably the decisive battlefield. Mr Atiku already beat Mr Tinubu in the North-East; the bigger, harder prize lies in Kano, Kaduna, Katsina, Jigawa, Kebbi, Sokoto and Zamfara.
https://dailytrust.com/2027-elections-10.title_zh: 2027年选举：1.03亿选民、3500万张选票，以及可能决定总统归属的68%选民
https://dailytrust.com/2027-elections-10.body_zh: 如果尼日利亚人像2023年那样投票，但有更多人出来投票，Aso Rock之争就会呈现截然不同的面貌。东南部、Kano的Kwankwaso政治机器、4个州逆转选情，以及一位地区新秀的影响，可能比任何选民心意的改变都更重要。不到100天，尼日利亚人将选出一名总统，其中大多数人正为不安全局势和不断飙升的生活成本所困扰。然而，此次选举存在一个悖论。选民人数比以往任何时候都多，候选人格局也更加分散，但结果可能更少取决于选民怎么想，而更多取决于他们中究竟谁真正投了票。先从数字说起。选民名册已从2023年的9350万增至1.034亿。《Vanguard》和《Stears》整理的上一次选举各州结果提供了基本图景。假定选民偏好不变——Tinubu选民仍投Tinubu，Atiku选民仍投Atiku，Obi选民仍投Obi，Kwankwaso选民仍投Kwankwaso——只改变投票率，这张图景便开始偏离实际情况。需要说明的是：这是一个情景推演，不是预测或民调。它把2026—27年的选民名册与2023年的各州得票率结合起来，再叠加一系列假设——设定投票率、Obi—Kwankwaso合并、互换Plateau、Osun、Taraba和Bayelsa的得票率，以及假设Makinde—Bala以APM平台参选Bauchi和Oyo。后文还会检验Tinubu先生与Atiku先生之间的直接转投。该模型也没有对选举舞弊进行调整。它无需调整：2023年的结果曾以存在违规行为为由一路诉至最高法院，并获维持。因此，无论当时发生了何种违规行为，都已经包含在这些推演所依据、且依法尘埃落定的基准结果之中。2023年，Peter Obi先生在南部部分地区取得巨大优势，但他的许多票仓最终仅是温和领先。相比之下，Bola Tinubu先生和Abubakar Atiku先生则在投票率很高的州吸引了大量选票。若将2023年全国投票率26.71%统一套用于新选民名册，算术结果显示，Tinubu先生获得960万票，Obi—Kwankwaso组合获得897万票，Atiku先生获得723万票。仅合并这一项就足以改变选情。更有意思的问题是，如果低投票率地区开始表现得像高投票率地区，会发生什么。以Anambra和Kano为例。假设Anambra选民不再重复2023年的低迷表现，而是达到大致与Kano相当的投票率。把这一情况推广至Obi先生2023年获胜的各州：设定31.7%的投票率下限，而在历史投票率本已高于这一水平的地区，则继续保留较高比率。结果发生逆转。Obi—Kwankwaso以1014万票略微领先Tinubu先生的1006万票，Atiku先生为751万票——领先优势仅约8.5万票。这应会让所有政党总部感到不安。Obi先生未必需要在2027年从数百万2023年支持Tinubu的选民中夺走胜果；他首先或许需要让自己的更多支持者走进投票站。双方都可以打这张牌。然而，如果对Atiku先生的各州也作同样处理，优势就会消失。Adamawa、Bauchi、Gombe、Kaduna、Katsina、Kebbi、Osun、Sokoto、Taraba、Yobe及其地盘内其他地区的投票率提高，对他并无单独帮助，因为他的对手在那里也获得了大量选票。Tinubu先生重新以约1105万票领先，Obi—Kwankwaso为1050万票，Atiku先生为883万票。对Tinubu先生的各州作同样处理，投票总数将升至3470万票左右，约占选民名册的33.6%：Tinubu先生1216万票，Obi—Kwankwaso 1079万票，Atiku先生951万票。执政者的结构性优势再次显现。教训在于：不能孤立地评估动员效果。如果所有人都能以同等程度参与投票，优势就会回到那个在地域覆盖、大州实力和体面的第二名成绩方面拥有最佳组合的联盟。选举并非简单重演，因此再加入一些选情变动。假设Obi先生2023年获胜的Plateau转向Tinubu先生；不凭空设定转投幅度，只互换两人的2023年得票率。对Atiku先生的3个州——Osun、Taraba和Bayelsa——也作同样处理，让它们向Tinubu先生偏移。Tinubu先生升至约1248万票，Obi—Kwankwaso降至1062万票，Atiku先生降至935万票。他的领先优势扩大到约186万票。4个州改变了整场选情的面貌。接下来是搅局者。再加入Makinde—Bala以APM平台参选，重点只在两个州布局：Bauchi，即Atiku先生2023年获胜的州，以及Oyo，即Tinubu先生的州。在这两个州，原胜者都降至第二，新入场者取得胜者份额。这使APM在Bauchi获得约58.4万票，在Oyo获得约60.1万票——仅凭两个州便获得约118万票。这变成了一场四方角逐。在完整情景下，投票总数达到约3500万票。Tinubu先生以1169万票获胜（33.67%），Obi—Kwankwaso获1062万票（30.58%），Atiku先生获896万票（25.79%），Makinde—Bala获118万票（3.41%）；其他候选人分得剩余的220万票（6.55%）。Tinubu先生仍然领先，但优势只略高于100万票。注意没有发生什么。没有人变出了一场选举革命。这项推演只是扩大了选民群体，略微推高了投票率，合并了两个阵营，移动了4个州，并增加了一名地区挑战者。然而，领先优势却易主，获胜差距也从8.5万票到186万票不等。很大程度上取决于投票率，东南部尤其如此。该地区5个州拥有约1198万名登记选民。但登记本身并不赋予任何影响力：待在家里的选民，与从未登记的选民影响完全相同。投票率可能才是2027年最关键的隐藏变量。Lagoos拥有近750万名登记选民。若投票率为31.7%，就意味着将投出近240万张选票。按2023年的得票率计算，Obi—Kwankwaso获得约105万票，Tinubu先生获得约102万票—— statistically两 statistically几乎持平。几万张选票的转移，就可能改变全国结果。Lagoos值得争取的不仅是胜利，而且是大幅获胜。这是如何输得漂亮的一门艺术。或许最反直觉的教训是，总统竞选并不是37场赢者通吃的竞争。一个候选人即使在某个州以45%对40%落败，仍能保留那40%的选票。赢得更多州，与在保持足够地域分布的同时把全国得票最大化，是两种不同的策略。造王者，而非王中之王。Makinde—Bala凭118万票远非位居第一，但其影响可能远超选票本身，因为这些选票并非平均分散：在Bauchi，它主要打击Atiku先生；在Oyo，它主要打击Tinubu先生。一名聚焦于恰到好处州份的小型第四候选人，能够施加与其全国份额远不相称的影响。最终位居第四的人，可能帮助决定谁位居第一。这个模型把选举归结为4场相互关联的较量。第一场围绕投票率：低参与率票仓能否在不引发对手同样增加投票的情况下投出更多选票？第二场围绕联盟：Obi—Kwankwaso之所以看似强大，是因为它把东南部、中部地带和Lagos的实力，与Kwankwaso先生在Kano的追随者结合起来。第三场涉及倒戈的州：Plateau、Osun、Taraba和Bayelsa表明，少量看似合理的选情转移，就可能净移动数十万张选票。第四场是搅局者之争，Makinde—Bala式组合虽在全国层面毫无竞争力，却能产生关键影响。这个数字令人不寒而栗。Tinubu先生最终略高于100万票的领先优势，只相当于1亿多选民名册的约1%。在登记选民中仅有约三分之一出来投票的情况下，如今不投票者中哪怕比例不高的人改变选择，也很容易淹没这点优势。仅靠互换选票和投票率变化无法做到这一点。令Tinubu先生无法被追平的临界比率会升至约121%——在数学上不可能实现。即使12个州的投票率都达到100%，Tinubu先生仍会以1802万票领先Atiku先生的1737万票，优势约65.6万票。为什么门槛如此之高？第一，新增投票是共享的：在2023年得票率固定不变的情况下，Tinubu先生和Obi—Kwankwaso也会增加得票，尤其是在Katsina、Kebbi、Sokoto、Osun和Bauchi，Tinubu先生在那里是颇具竞争力的第二名。第二，在APM于Bauchi取得胜者份额后，当地投票率越高，对Makinde—Bala的帮助就大于对Atiku先生的帮助。第三，在Bayelsa、Osun和Taraba，Tinubu先生如今拥有更大得票率，因此当地每多一名投票者，都会扩大他的领先优势。在发生100万张选票转移时，Tinubu先生与Obi—Kwankwaso之间的差距约为7.5万票，Atiku先生仍居第三。只有转移规模达到约200万票，他才能明确领先，届时领先Obi—Kwankwaso约33.9万票，领先Tinubu先生约126万票。关键在于“净”字。每一名从南部转投Tinubu先生的Atiku选民，都会使北部的追赶要求增加一人：若在南部失去50万票，他就需要约216万张选票完成转换，相当于Tinubu先生2023年北部选票的38.6%；若失去100万票，就需要266万张（47.5%）。即使没有南部失票，要取得一场稳稳当当的50万票胜利，也需要约216万张选票发生转换。把尼日利亚划分为北部的Atiku选区和南部的Tinubu选区颇具诱惑，但算术结果要复杂得多。2023年，Tinubu先生在北部19个州及联邦首都领区仅领先Atiku先生约36.5万票，而在南部的领先约为146万票。再把北部进一步拆分，情况就会更鲜明。在西北部和东北部——即“核心北部”——Atiku先生实际上以约23.4万票获胜。这掩盖了两场不同的较量：Tinubu先生在西北部领先约32.3万票，Atiku先生在东北部领先约55.6万票。换言之，“Atiku拿下北部、Tinubu拿下南部”在很大程度上就是2023年的实际格局。Atiku先生的问题在于规模：Tinubu先生在南部的领先优势超过其核心北部优势的6倍。两个阵营之间横亘着北中部，这里不应被视为核心北部的附属地区。2023年，该地区选票由三方瓜分：Tinubu先生获约176万票，Obi先生和Kwankwaso先生合计约148万票，Atiku先生约116万票。Tinubu先生拿下Benue、Kogi、Kwara和Niger；Obi先生赢得Nasarawa、Plateau和联邦首都领区。这里既有倾向APC的地区、PDP的传统票仓、强大的Obi支持者基础，也有族裔和宗教构成多元的选民群，因此是真正的摇摆地带。如果Tinubu先生在北中部的选票有10%转投Atiku先生，将移动约17.6万张选票，并把两人正面对决的差距改变约35.2万票——意义显著，但单凭这一变化仍不足以决定胜负。它的杠杆作用在于放大核心北部的收复，或保护南方领先优势。现在剔除投票率提升、选票互换和搅局者，回到最简单的基准情景：按各州在1.034亿选民名册中的份额套用26.71%的投票率，同时维持2023年各州得票率。三个战场合计投出约2760万张选票。2023年的格局依然存在，但规模发生变化。Atiku先生在核心北部的领先缩小至约13.2万票，而Tinubu先生在南部的领先扩大至近190万票——是前者的14倍以上。北中部也远非中立：它又为Tinubu先生贡献了61万票。在南部尚未投出任何一票之前，他已在北部和联邦首都领区领先约47.9万票。现在测试一种对称的重新结盟：Tinubu先生在核心北部的一部分选民转投Atiku先生，同时Atiku先生在南部同样比例的选民转投Tinubu先生，北中部保持不变。相同的百分比并不意味着相同的人数。Tinubu先生的核心北部选民池（388万）几乎是Atiku先生南部选民池（210万）的两倍，因此10%的转投意味着约38.8万名北部选民转投Atiku先生，而只有约21万名南部选民转投Tinubu先生。悖论在于，两人在国家的不同半区都会变得更强。转投比例达到15%时，Atiku先生以近130万票领先核心北部，但Tinubu先生仍以约252万票领先南部，并以约184万票领先全国。凭借规模更大的选民池，Atiku先生缩小了差距，但速度缓慢：在两个阵营之间，持平所需的转投比例约为49.4%——这意味着Tinubu先生核心北部近一半支持者倒戈，同时Atiku先生在南部相同比例的选票转向另一边。这不是选情摇摆，而是阵营重组；即便如此，Tinubu先生在北中部拥有的61万票缓冲仍将保留。因此，北部收复对Atiku先生是必要的，却还不充分：他还必须阻止PDP在Rivers、Oyo、Ogun、Akwa Ibom及其他地区残留的南方选票流失。由此，北西部可以说才是决定性战场。Atiku先生已经在东北部击败Tinubu先生；规模更大、更难攻取的目标则在Kano、Kaduna、Katsina、Jigawa、Kebbi、Sokoto和Zamfara。
